name: A CSWA CHRISTMAS: Where Dreams Really Do Come True

date.source: the document's own dateline, "December 25, 1995"

matches.note: To win, a wrestler had to put his opponent in the coffin at ringside and cover him head to toe with dirt. Space God was knocked out by petrified pig filth thrown from the crowd and fell into the coffin; ringside fans, referee Manuel Juarez and commentator Sammy Benson all shovelled filth in, and Benson chairshotted Devastator and emptied the dirt bag before Juarez called for the bell.

Billed in the match header as <> Cutters vs. Disco Express. Buckley introduces the Cutters as the EN/CPUWA World Tag Team champions but the document does not say the belts were at stake. Enderson knocked out the Boogie Man with brass knuckles, hit a DDT and hid the knucks in Boogie Man's tights before the count.

For the USN Heavyweight Title. Referee Ben Worthington was knocked down; Mark Windham came out, hit his brother Timmy with an Implant DDT and the claw on the floor, piledrove an unaware Scotty Michaels, then draped Michaels over Timmy. Worthington revived and counted the fall. Michaels was reported not to know at first that he had won the belt.

Billed in the header as The Armed Forces vs. Samson/Chain. Side bet announced by Rhubarb Jones: Samson wins $500,000 from TTL if he can SummerSlam Battleship, and loses $500,000 if he tries and fails. Samson had Battleship up when Submarine ran in and clipped his knee; Battleship fell on top of him for the three count and TTL collected the money.

matches.note: Short form; 'Loki's grapevine cover ended the match with a win for the big man.' Loki ranked #23, Bramble a former ABWA World Champion.
Silver's CSWA debut, billed as a member of the FIRST FAMILY of James Cornette. 'Winner:  JOHNNY SILVER.'
Billed as a 'tune-up' for Delerious's tournament match; won with a Neckbreaker, knee lift and HEAVY SEDITION DDT.
Thorn's CSWA debut, also billed FIRST FAMILY; 'The Termination torture rack finisher of Thorn's led to Prosser's submission.'
'Iron Eagle has defeated Steven Flair in the biggest upset we've seen in the CSWA in a long time' - jump-splash cover off the top.

Royal Fashion billed as Sir Dunton and the Model; Simply Irresistible, debuting, as 'Gorgeous' Greg Brant and 'Irresistible' Eddie Blake. Ref Pee Wee Troutman counted Dunton's back slide on Blake. A later 'Note to members' in the source restates the finish, the poster being unsure whether the match had been posted.

name: BATTLE OF THE BELTS XIII: Super Bowl Blast '96

date.source: the document's own dateline, "February 3, 1996"

matches.note: Opening bout, called live. Lewis blocked a suplex and turned it into an inside cradle.
Shown on tape, joined in progress; billed by Buckley as a match that happened earlier the same night before the broadcast went on the air, not an archival replay. Second-rope elbow drop for the fall.
Shown on tape, joined in progress; same-night pre-broadcast match. Mcidiot tripped over Gage and was rolled up.
Finished with the SummerSlam.
HeartBreaker pulled brass knuckles; Starr blocked the shot, took the knucks and used them himself. Announcers acknowledge it and let the result stand.

Billed as Masters of Misery vs Japanese Assault; recapped in short form. Shogun superkicked Hurt then tagged the Kid for a SWAN DIVE, a little after the 20 minute mark. Japanese Assault are part of the Rosenthal Family.
Brawled to the back; announced as a double countout. No draw or no-contest wording used, so no result field recorded.
Billed as Armed Forces vs Disco Express, with the Disco/Red Midget at ringside. Winners were announced as receiving a tag title shot at the UNIFIED, EN or US tag titles on the next card.
Top-rope shoulderblock after Viper countered the Powerbomb.
Japanese Assault's second win of the night. Wild Asian and Bandit ran in with trash cans; referee Ben Worthington called for the bell and awarded Japanese Assault the win by disqualification.

Both men billed as debuting in the CSWA this night. Scotty/Shawn Matthews superkicked Gage on the floor out of referee Manuel Juarez' sight, then rolled him in for MTV; announcers call it a pre-arranged act between Matthews and MTV.
For the Greensboro Title. Praxis defending, managed by Dr.Guggan with the wheel barrow. Won with a crucifix; Benson claims Asian had the tights.

For the USN Heavyweight Title. Vince Bailey came out mid-match and offered Chain $50,000 to withdraw from Ultratitle; Chain refused, and the briefcase became a weapon. Sammy Benson stole the briefcase from ringside. Teri Melton appears to have rung the bell to break up Chain's three count, then handed Michaels a high heel shoe; Michaels used it for the finish. Juarez missed it.

For the EN/CPUWA World Tag Team Title. Billed as <>Cutters (champions, with Maxwell Diamond) vs CS Express. Planchard used a metal object wrapped in a fan's jersey; Worthington called for the bell and the Cutters were disqualified, so the Express win the match but the Cutters keep the belts. Diamond then counted his own mock pinfalls over both Express members.

For the EN World Heavyweight Title. Billed as a rematch, contested on Death Island with the Dallas crowd watching on the big screen; no DQ. Randalls' Army of Darkness (Hellstalker and two cloaked men) interfered. GUNS won by submission with the Scorpion Deathlock, described as his Secret Weapon and credited to Hornet. Afterward Randalls levelled GUNS with the EN belt and took his Hornet armband.

For the CSWA US TAG CHAMPIONSHIP. Billed as NC-17 vs Carl Brigsby/Wesley Paige. The Armed Forces had been scheduled for this shot but stepped aside on joining the Corporation. Brigsby tripped over the top turnbuckle, flipped in midair and landed on Wildstar for the pin. Ray S. Cornette then fired NC-17 and the Armed Forces destroyed them.

For the Intracontinental Title. Eliminator defending, accompanied by his wife Alicia. Doc Silver and Hell's Caretaker came to the aisle and Alicia collapsed; Hornet ran out and Ivy left the booth. Hornet pulled Eli out of the way of Bandit's tope, Bandit hit the barricade, and Eli hooked the leg for three, then immediately left the ring.

For the UNIFIED TAG TEAM TITLE. Billed as Dream Team vs Horsemen, Horsemen defending. Mike Flair interfered with a chair. Teri Melton distracted Scotty Michaels; Lex Taylor abandoned a pin to confront them and Chain rolled him up with a handful of tights. Taylor then struck referee Ben Worthington.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "July 12, 1996"

matches.note: Outlaw jumped Starr before the bell; ref Ben Worthington finally called for it. Starr worked the previously injured right arm with a chicken wing and finished with a superplex from the top.
Under five minutes. The recap opens "A couple of words could sum this one up: no contest" as a figure of speech for a squash, then declares a winner.

Headed "DIVISION I" in the served copy, but Buckley immediately afterwards says Starr "has run the WINNING STREAK in Division II, defeating Outlaw and Kaleidoscope". Starr held a step-over-toe hold for almost ten minutes and pinned Kaleidoscope after flipping over him.

No "WINNER:" line is printed, but the recap states Asian's top rope Frank n' Parsons "put Mitchell down for the three-count", and Asian is subsequently named the Division I winner going into the final.

For the UNIFIED World Tag Team Championships. Billed as Disco Express vs. Japanese Assault, the number three contenders. The Disco Midget distracted ref Ben Worthington for the champions; Matt Rosenthal returned from Japan and came to ringside mid-match. Japanese Assault won with the KAMIKAZE SHOTGUN. Afterwards the Disco Midget decked the Boogie Man.

For the Intracontinental Championship. Refereed by Patrick Young. Teri Melton came to ringside for Starr, distracted the referee and grabbed Starr's leg; the recap then jumps to Starr strapping on the belt, with Wild Asian carted away by paramedics after a missed moonsault "which he owes to Teri Melton". Starr thereby held the Greensboro and Intracontinental titles at once, which Buckley says he will have to give up one of.

For the Greensboro Championship. Impromptu: Scott Waters ran down immediately after the Winning Streak final, pushed Teri Melton aside and attacked Starr, and Buckley says "apparently, the title for the Greensboro Championship is underway". Melton hit Waters with a chair. The two brawled over the barricade into the first rows of seats and referee Young called for the bell. No ruling is given.

matches.stipulation: EN WORLD/US TAG TEAM TOURNEY FINALS
matches.note: For the EN WORLD TAG TEAM CHAMPIONS. Billed as Generation X-Press vs. The FORCE; the X-Press's third match of the night against the FORCE's first. Refereed by Pee Wee Troutman. A double pin finish — HEAT and Waters double-powerbombed Matthews while Troy Windham bulldogged Waters — with Rhubarb Jones announcing the X-Press as winners after conferring with Troutman. The runners-up, The FORCE, took the US Tag Team titles.

Billed as CS EXPRESS vs. <> CUTTERS, a grudge match. Jason Palmer and Dr.Thomas Knight ran down the aisle mid-match — Buckley protests "They're not in the CSWA!" — distracting Morton on top of the cage. Enderson threw Morton down for a SPIKED PILEDRIVER and Planchard covered. The second time the Cutters have pinned the CS Express.

For the EN WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT TITLE. Billed as "MARK WINDHAM VS RUDY'S MYSTERY MAN"; Rudy Seizter revealed the challenger as the masked SEAHAWK, brought in with clearance from the AAWC. Windham removed the floor padding and piledrove him on the concrete, then covered him with one finger. Windham retained and the Seahawk was left motionless.

For the USN Title. Refereed by Worthington. Michaels caught Worthington in a headlock while Teri Melton came off the top rope, hit Reno low and then delivered a Top Rope DDT; Michaels finished with a leg drop off the middle rope.

Hornet attacked before the bell, threw referee Ben Worthington out of the cage, took his key and padlocked the door. He hit a Shooting Star Press and applied the SCORPION DEATHLOCK while Mark Windham pulled Maxwell Diamond off the outside of the cage and applied the iron claw. Hornet released the hold, unlocked the door and left with Windham. Buckley states flatly "The match never got started, Red"; Red Midget insists Hornet "won the match.... thoroughly". No ruling is given, and Bailey was later reported taken to hospital.

Three stacked cages with the WHEEL mounted on top; whichever team gets two or three of its members strapped into the WHEEL officially loses. FULL FORCE (Miles and Collins) attacked before Randalls appeared, injuring Mister Self-Destruct (cracked rib) with a chair. Collins strapped Goliath in; Eliminator strapped Collins in; Randalls then swung down from the rafters with Alicia — the Eliminator's wife — dropkicked Eli off the cage and strapped her in as the third body, starting the WHEEL. The document declares no winner. Reported injuries: Goliath, major contusions and broken ribs; Alicia, mino

date.source: the document's own dateline, "May 13, 1999"

matches.stipulation: UNIFIED TAG TEAM CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, QUARTERFINALS (#1 vs #9)
matches.note: Disco Inferno and Boogie Man with the Disco Midget against Stellar Stan and Galactic Grant with William H. Bradley III. Stellar Stan rolled up Boogie Man and hooked the tights for the three.

matches.stipulation: UNIFIED TAG TEAM CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, QUARTERFINALS (#3 vs #5)
matches.note: Peyton Wright and Joey Melton with Ray S. Cornette and Teri Melton against Blade and Dante Inferno with Silky Rose. While referee Ben Worthington broke up Silky Rose's attack on Teri Melton, Inferno chokeslammed and spiked Melton and Blade dropped Wright across the guardrail. Worthington awarded the match to Razor Meltdown on returning his attention to the ring.

matches.stipulation: UNIFIED TAG TEAM CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, QUARTERFINALS (#2 vs #10)
matches.note: Susan and Gina distracted referee Patrick Young while Sweet Melissa tossed Kevin Powers the steel-plated bat; Powers connected and covered.

matches.stipulation: UNIFIED TAG TEAM CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, QUARTERFINALS (#4 vs #6)
matches.note: No contest took place. Vice-Commissioner Vizzachero informed the officials that the Privateers had not shown up to the building, and Rhubarb Jones announced Black Army advancing by default.

For the CSWA UNITED STATES HEAVYWEIGHT TITLE. K-9 handled Nemesis' ring introduction. Rudy Seitzer interrupted to reveal via blood tests and birth certificates that Nemesis and K-9 are blood brothers, sons of Carol Wallace. In the match K-9 handed Nemesis a chair and Worthington counted a three; junior referee Patrick Young reported the chair and the match was restarted. Radder then hit the Absolute Zero for the win. Afterward Kelly told Radder she is pregnant.

matches.stipulation: UNIFIED TAG TEAM CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, SEMIFINALS (#9 vs #5)
matches.note: Mark Vizzack came out and drew Dante Inferno out of the ring after Inferno tagged Blade in; William H. Bradley III hooked Blade's ankle and Stan and Grant used chairs, then hit a double chokeslam for the fall.

matches.stipulation: UNIFIED TAG TEAM CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, SEMIFINALS (#2 vs #4)
matches.note: Sweet Melissa slipped Eddy Love the baseball bat while Susan had Ben Worthington's attention; Love hit Pat Black in the head and finished with the Hurricane Piledriver. After the match an unidentified woman jumped from the crowd and threw a fireball into Susan's face.

matches.stipulation: "Ladders and Weapons" - no rules, any weapon legal
matches.note: For the CSWA GREENSBORO TITLE. Rhubarb Jones announced the only way to win was to ascend the ladder and retrieve the belt, but the finish was a pinfall. Hornet, who had been guest commentating, left the table, pulled Harders off a cover and hit him with a chair; Douglas laid an arm over him for the three. Described as Harders' first CSWA defeat and Douglas' second Greensboro reign.

matches.stipulation: FINALS; titles vacant, so a Disqualification or Countout would also be grounds for crowning champions
matches.note: For the UNIFIED TAG TEAM CHAMPIONSHIP. With Ben Worthington down, Eddy Love hit the Hurricane Piledriver on Galactic Grant and Kevin Powers hit Kiss the Canvas on Stellar Stan for a double pin that Worthington counted on recovering.

matches.stipulation: special attraction MIXED TAG TEAM MATCH, NO TIME LIMIT, masked guest referee
matches.note: The masked referee kept both sides apart with Ivy's confiscated Singapore Cane. Hornet had Vizzack in a modified Scorpion Deathlock and Buckley believed the match was over, but the referee did not call for the bell; he unmasked as Eli Flair and caned Hornet, Ivy and then Hornet again. Billy Starr came from the crowd with a chair to go after Flair. No finish and no ruling.

matches.note: Impromptu. WildStar and Tsunami - "DAWN OF A NEW DAY" - appear out of a blackout as Brigsby and Page corner Teri Melton, and referee Pee Wee Troutman runs down to make it a match. Finished with the Wild Driver and a Tsunami shooting star press.
Madara's introduction match; Stanley called for the bell himself. Madara gave up almost immediately to a surfboard.

Challenge issued in the ring by Ian Squeezefeld (Ill Squeeze), who demanded Cardigo lie down and be pinned. Cardigo instead hit three one-handed chokeslams and covered. Afterwards he piledrove the sixty-five year old Thornton Squeezefeld off the top rope and jabbed a fork into Ian's forehead before police escorted him out.
X finished with a springboard hurricanrana into a cradle.

Beretta put up ten thousand dollars for any "legend" and chose Curiously Bruce, a bearded midget wrestler. Troutman counted quickly to keep Beretta from pulling him up again. Broderick Jones openly objects to the match and to WildStar's language about Bruce.

Three-way. Erik Jackson was pulled out of the match early when a goth fan hopped the railing and hit him in the neck with a billyclub; the fan named himself Stevie Calhoun, was let into the ring by security at Haggar's own request, and wrestled the rest of the match in Jackson's place. The bout ended when the PA announced thirty seconds remaining and the referee told Calhoun the time limit was up mid-count; Calhoun hit a cradle piledriver anyway and the referee called for the bell. No winner is declared.

For the Greensboro Title. Blade dropped the belt on the mat and tried to walk out; Sunshine Del Payne told him he would be suspended indefinitely if he did not wrestle, and rang the bell herself. Blade chokeslammed referee Patrick Young for the disqualification, then backhanded Del Payne, drawing Mark Windham out. Del Payne ruled Blade had vacated the title before the match, making Wicked Sight the new champion.

For the Unified Tag Team Championship. MAIN EVENT. Love revealed Troy Windham, not Deacon, as his partner - the two announce themselves as "The Playboys" and reveal a plot going back to Day 1; Deacon and Shepherd were ambushed by three masked men (Windham, Junior Hornet, Bandit). Powers' partner was revealed as his arch-rival Apocalypse. Both teams collapsed after a Hurricane Piledriver and a top-rope powerbomb through a table; Melissa dragged the fallen Juarez over, both men were draped for covers, and Juarez counted three and handed both tag belts to Kevin Powers.

name: CSWA ANNIVERSARY 1996: Hot Southern Days and Rock and Roll Nights

date.source: the card's own header, "3/31/96".

matches.note: Day One. Tidle Wave billed as a newcomer; won after a splash off the ropes.
Day One. Heartbreaker won with a superkick.
Day One. Won by stripping the opponent's tuxedo; Ivy took Melton's top off last. Melton chaired Ivy repeatedly afterwards before officials separated them.

Day One. Wild Asian missed a reverse moonsault through a ringside table and landed neck-first; Reno refused to continue and referee Patrick Young called for the bell and awarded the match to Reno. Buckley then reports Reno shaking his head and refusing to take the win that way. Wild Asian was stretchered out; Stan Parsons reported later on the card from Wesley Long Hospital that it was only a stinger and no serious damage was done.

For the Intracontential Title. Day One, billed as Intracontential Title Defense. MTV is managed by Matt Rosenthal. Eliminator retained with a TR Clothesline off the top. Wrestling without Poison Ivy, who had gone to the hospital with the Wild Asian. One line of play-by-play mistakenly calls MTV 'Reno'.

For the GREENSBORO CHAMPIONSHIP. Day One. Billed as Starr's first defence after winning the belt from the Wild Asian at WINTER WARRIOR'S VII. Gage was seconded by Lady Luck, who placed his arm on the ropes to break a Scorpion Deathlock. Starr retained with a dragon suplex.

Day One. Stipulation was that anyone pinned or submitting leaves the CSWA for three months. Flair was ambushed before the bell by the disguised 'TERMINATOR' TODD MITCHELL and beaten down by Scotty Michaels and Teri Melton, then chokeslammed, and was carried through the match. Referee Patrick Young called for the bell when Steel Viper set up a table on the floor, giving Flair a disqualification win; Viper then put him through the table with a Vipersault and Flair was stretchered out.
Day One, billed as one half of the double main event. Teri Melton put Michaels' foot on the ropes to break one count and then held GUNS' leg down during the winning fall after a Michaels superkick.
Day One. Mark Windham hosted a public workout instead of defending the EN World Title, with Hornet at ringside and Patrick Young officiating. Worthington gave up to the Torture Rack.
Day One. Zeke Weasel had Windham beaten until Hornet tripped him from the floor; Windham won with an Implant DDT.

Day One. Hornet introduced Pierce, billed as the HWA US Heavyweight champion and a former CSWL find, as a surprise workout opponent. No finish: the two brawled, Windham went for a chair, Hornet took it away, Windham shoved Pierce down and left with Hornet.

Day One main event. Waters was jumped on the aisle by Vince Bailey, Maxwell Diamond and the <> Cutters, and Tom Adler joined in, revealing himself as back with the <> X-Change. Fall one to Adler by Adlerplex; fall two to Waters by TR bulldog off the top; in the third fall Vince Bailey put on a loaded glove and knocked Waters out on the floor while Diamond distracted the referee, and Waters was counted out.
Day Two. Billed as Eddie Lawerence's CSWA debut; managed by Miss Tori. Won with a small package.
Day Two. Lunacy won with a flying body press off the top.
Day Two. Reno, managed by Rosenthal, won with a Perfectplex.
Day Two. Written up in recap form ending 'Winner: THE TECHNICIAN'.
Day Two. Billed in the header as Masters of Misery vs. NC-17. Called an upset; the Masters of Misery were already in line for a tag title shot via a win in the Triangular tag match.

Day Two. Billed in the header as Japanese Assault vs. S&M (the header is printed twice, in both orders). Japanese Assault are billed as members of the Rosenthal family. The Kamikaza Kid won it with a reverse moonsault.

Day Two. Matt Rosenthal twice interfered for Dennison; Dennison won after hitting Matthews in the head with his pitchfork behind the referee's back. The commentary calls Matthews 'Shawn' once and 'Michaels' once in error.
Day Two. Billed in the header as CS EXPRESS vs. The MASKED ASSASSINS. Won with a Rocket Launcher.

Day Two. Billed as no rules, everything goes. Razorback bladed Anarky with a boot spur; Anarky used his own boot as a weapon. Razorback won with a roll-up after Anarky missed a flying bodypress into the cage.

For the INTRACONTINENTAL CHAMPIONSHIP. Day Two. Rematch of a bout ATTAXX had apparently won, whose decision was overturned by Co-commissioner Chad Merritt. A baseball bat hung on a pole and whoever retrieved it could use it; ATTAXX got it and hit Eli, but Eli took it off him and powerbombed him onto it for the win. Immediately afterwards the Eliminator took the house mic and threw the belt down, vacating a title he had held almost eight months.

For the PRESIDENTIAL CHAMPIONSHIP. Day Two, written up in short form at the writer's own note that he was unwell. Chain is marked <C> as champion. Jimmy Ray Vaughn interfered for Chain; Samson still ducked the Lethal Injection and won with a flying crossbody, then was laid out after the match by Chain and Vaughn.

matches.stipulation: Chad Merritt and Maxwell Diamond locked in SEPARATE CAGES and hoisted 35 FEET above the ring
matches.note: For the UNIFIED WORLD TAG TEAM CHAMPIONSHIP. Day Two, written up in short form. Named wrestlers are Disco Inferno and the Boogie Man for the champions and Tully Planchard and Ern Enderson for the challengers; the header bills only the team names. Maxwell Diamond dropped brass knuckles from his cage but Co-Commissioner Stephen Thomas grabbed them first; in the confusion Disco Inferno tagged himself in and rolled Enderson up for the three.

Day Two main event. No finish is announced. Hornet lured Randalls in, Mark Windham ran in and clipped his knee, then Hornet signalled for 'Golden Boy' Paul Pierce, who joined the three-on-one attack; Hornet applied the Scorpion Deathlock and Pierce hit Randalls with a coal miner's glove. Windham and Hornet argued with Pierce and all three left. Buckley closed the broadcast without any ruling.

name: CSWA ANNIVERSARY 1997: Nine Years In The Making

date.source: the fed's own Backpage archive index of its own cards (/promotions/cswa/archive/the-backpage-cswa-archives-january-2001-2001-01-02.html), which files it as "CSWA ANNIVERSARY 1997: Nine Years In The Making", 4/28/97.

matches.note: Troy Windham accompanied by Jimmy V., who used the ropes for leverage, choked GUNS behind referee Pee Wee Troutman's back and finally cracked GUNS with a loaded leather boot; GUNS powerbombed him. Mark Windham then came down the aisle in a black trench coat and yellow sun glasses, clotheslined and piledrove Troy on the concrete, propped him on the top rope and walked out; GUNS, who never saw Windham, hit a top rope belly to belly for the pin.

Refereed by Patrick Young. Masked Man #3 hit a flying dropkick off the barricade that sent Massacre head-first into the ring post, then a brainbuster on the concrete; Massacre was busted open and counted out. After the bell Masked Man #3 cracked Massacre with a chair until Troy Martinez and Jared Justice ran him off.

For the CSWA World Heavyweight Championship. Masked Man #3 took the microphone before the bell and pulled off the black covering, revealing himself as JULIUS GODREIGN. Refereed by Ben Worthington. GUNS escaped a sleeper and finished with a TOMBSTONE PILEDRIVER. As the losing finalist Godreign takes the USN Heavyweight title; he grabbed a chair and then a microphone, telling GUNS "You got lucky today, son... it's not over.."

name: CSWA ANNIVERSARY 1998: Titanic - Sink or Swim

date.source: the document's own dateline, "April 12, 1998"

matches.note: For the Unified World Tag Titles. Billed teams: Killer Instinct vs. Swat Team. Referee Patrick Young was knocked out by a Troy Martinez clothesline off the top; Joey Melton then ran down and teed off on Martinez's head with a golf club, busting him open, before Beretta hit the Holster Steiner Screwdriver.

Mark Windham had not been seen in the building and came out of the crowd during Troy's promo. He chaired commentator Sammy Benson at the desk and superplexed Troy through a table. Junior Hornet ran in and was piledriven and racked. Shawn Matthews came over the railing and handed Troy a can of mace, which Troy sprayed into Mark's eyes before the Double Arm Powerbomb.
Introduced by Rhubarb Jones. Referee Ben Worthington. Randalls finished with a brainbuster from the top rope.

For the CSWA World Heavyweight Championship. Billed as the MAIN EVENT, "One More Time...", with the vacant World Title on the line. Referee Ben Worthington. GUNS took the first fall with a top rope splash after roughly thirty minutes; Hornet took the second with a modified inside cradle out of the Scorpion. Past the hour mark Troy Windham pulled GUNS outside and Mark Windham chaired Hornet in the back, after which GUNS and Hornet turned on both Windhams together. Rhubarb Jones ruled the third fall a no-contest, leaving the match a draw at one fall apiece and the title vacant.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "July 25, 1999"

matches.note: First IRONMAN of CHAMPIONS tournament match. Deacon pins Hornet with the Altar Call for twenty points. Afterward Randy Harders and Pat Black head for the ring but a masked man in black descends from the rafters and levels them both with a crowbar.
Vizzack counters a powerbomb into the Frank'n'Parsons for the pin, going nearly the thirty-minute limit; he reinjures his shoulder on the finish.

Referee Patrick Young is knocked down twice. Poison Ivy canes Love in the head and later pins the cane across his throat in the corner for the Hornet Splash; Sweet Melissa had earlier thumbed Hornet in the eye. Hornet drags Young over and hooks the leg for the three.
Vizzack's shoulder is taped; Deacon drops to his knees on the Daredevil Flyer and covers. Deacon moves to 40 points and into first place; EMTs come to the ring for Vizzack.
Vizzack's second match in a row, wrestled against medical advice; Powers works the shoulder throughout and finishes with KISS THE CANVAS. Vizzack is announced as mathematically eliminated.
Vizzack's third match in a row. Love catches a shooting star press and powerbombs him, then covers with a foot on the middle rope. Sunshine Del Payne and Sweet Melissa trade slaps at ringside.
Love jumps Flair before the introductions finish. Steve Radder appears on the apron and distracts Love off the top rope; Flair superplexes him through a table for the pin. Referee Pee Wee Troutman.

Powers pulls referee Ben Worthington into Deacon's path, then produces brass knuckles; Deacon blocks and chokeslams him, but Worthington spots the knucks lying by Deacon and disqualifies the Deacon instead. Powers takes 10 points and 30 total. Shepherd protests.

Jesse Solomon interferes repeatedly against Flair, takes Shepherd's crook to Flair's back, then chairs Deacon when Deacon dives in front of Shepherd. Flair rolls Deacon back inside rather than take the countout and pins him with a belly-to-belly. Ties the standings at 40; Deacon eliminated.

Hornet dropkicks Powers' already-injured knee before the bell is properly called and works it all match; Powers' knee gives out on the Power Outage attempt. Submission to the Scorpion Deathlock, referee Pee Wee Troutman calling for the bell.

Sweet Melissa slides in a chair and puts Love's foot on the rope on a near fall; referee Pee Wee Troutman is knocked down. Powers finally muscles Love up butterfly-style and drops him on his head. Powers moves to fifty points and the lead.

matches.stipulation: cage lowered over the ring; billed as 'THE FINAL CHAPTER'
matches.note: Billed Timmy Windham vs Mark Windham. Sammy Benson attacks ring announcer Rhubarb Jones and self-appoints as announcer. Sunshine Del Payne dumps Mickey Benedict from his wheelchair, revealing he can walk, and rolls him into the ring; Mark handcuffs Timmy to the ropes and the cage traps Benedict inside, so the bout runs mostly as Mark Windham vs Mickey Benedict. Referee Ben Worthington calls for the bell after Mark elbow-drops Benedict from the top of the cage, but NO winner is announced anywhere in this copy. Benedict says 'I QUIT' after the bell, under duress. Timmy is hip-tossed off the cage

For the CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP. Both men entered at 40 points; a pinfall win took the vacant World Title. Poison Ivy walks out with Flair instead of Hornet, produces a pair of women's underwear and canes Hornet; Hornet admits an affair with Jewels Windham. Hornet hits a shooting star press and takes the microphone believing he has won, but referee Manuel Juarez had seen Flair's boot on the lower rope; Juarez restarts the match, Ivy canes Hornet again, and Flair pins him with an inverted DDT.

name: CSWA INDEPENDENCE DAY 2000 -- July 20, 2000

date.source: the document's own dateline, "July 20, 2000"

matches.note: Billed as Evan Aho vs. Shawn "Superman" Stevens. Referee Patrick Young informed Rhubarb Jones that contractual problems between Stevens, the CSWA and the SCW meant Stevens could not compete; Kerry Allen, back from Japan, replaced him. Aho finished with The Agony into The Ecstasy, a Tiger Driver '91.
Cancer is identified as the former Pat Black of the UnHoly. Cisco won by submission with the Ciscolating End after the Hallow Point sky high splash.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "May 28, 1999"

matches.note: Cool Moe D scored the pinfall in fifteen minutes with a powerbomb after nearly losing early.

Eli Flair came to ringside and watched; when Pyro told him to leave, Flair clocked him with a right hand and Knuckles hit a DDT for the three. Flair then cut a promo staking his claim to the sixth IRONMAN slot.

The Hooded Falcon returned, ran to ringside and was invited by Wicked Sight to strike Solomon with his cane; Solomon ducked and Sight took the blow. Solomon rolled him in for the pin as the Falcon was hoisted away on a guywire.
Rematch of the Orlando time-limit draw. Referee Ben Worthington ruled it a win for Wells though many fans thought Dexter got the shoulder up before three.
Senior referee Pee Wee Troutman officiating. Apocalypse came out with Miso, who led the blinded Susan to the ring on a leash and tied her to the ropes. Finish was a powerbomb into the Seventh Seal.

God's Protege leveled Deacon as he reached for a tag and the rest of the Unholy swarmed. Apocalypse then welcomed Randy Harders and God's Protege into the group and had them beat down K-9, before the Unholy turned on both K-9 and Nemesis. Miso and Silky Rose fireballed the brothers in the eyes and Apocalypse declared them "FIRED". No finish and no ruling.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "July 14, 1999"

matches.note: Finished with The Show Stopper in under five minutes; described as a message to the rest of the Battle Royal participants.

matches.stipulation: "Rookie" Battle Royal - winner gets a shot at the Greensboro Title
matches.note: Eleven men. A masked man attacked Lawrence Stanley on the way to the ring. Eliminations in order: Duke Williams (X-Rated), Michael Hardy, Wicked Sight (returned through the ropes, later eliminated by Stanley), Jesse Solomon, X-Rated (HaVoC), Simon Wilcox and Matt Dexter, then Wicked Sight, then Rob Sampson and HaVoC together. The last two, Alex Wylde and Lawrence Stanley, went over the top together when Wylde superplexed Stanley to the floor; Stanley through a table, Wylde onto the ring steps. No winner declared in this document.

For the CSWA Greensboro Championship. Referee Manny Juarez. The arena lost power during the match and Blade used a steel chair; after a Guillotine Blade a 'cameraman' pulled Blade off the cover and revealed himself as Cool Moe D, who renamed himself "The Monarch" Matt Martin and called out Genocide. Genocide appeared and the two brawled until security separated them.

For the CSWA United States Championship. Harders defending. Referee Patrick Young had threatened Hornet with disqualification for brass knuckles. Both men were counted out while Buckley's table was occupied with Vice-Commisioner Vizzachero signing Poison Ivy to a contract to sit out ANNIVERSARY in exchange for her old column space. Ivy then attacked Harders.

Billed as The Powers of Love vs. Mark Vizzack and Deacon; with Deacon and Sunshine missing, Vizzack announced Mark Windham as his new partner. Sweet Melissa's heel shot busted Powers open. Miso appeared with Susan on a leash and Apocalypse tackled Powers; Steve Radder came from the crowd and chaired Eddy Love; Hornet, Timmy Windham and Eli Flair all joined in. Deacon and Sunshine Del Payne then returned, Deacon chokeslamming Love and Hornet. No finish and no ruling.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "January 11, 1999"

matches.stipulation: Greensboro World Cup Quarterfinals, Bracket A
matches.note: Apocalypse accompanied by Lady Death; finished with a chokeslam and the Seventh Seal at the 3 minute mark. Afterwards he chokeslammed Sgt. Stalker and Sgt. Chenoski onto the guardrail.

matches.stipulation: Greensboro World Cup Quarterfinals, Bracket A
matches.note: Described as a low-energy match with the fans chanting "BOOOORING"; God's Protege finished after ten minutes with a spike piledriver.

matches.stipulation: Greensboro World Cup Quarterfinals, Bracket B
matches.note: Ray S. Cornette accidentally tripped Jaminson on a reversed Irish whip, and Mysterious took the three count with a belly-to-belly suplex.

matches.stipulation: Greensboro World Cup Quarterfinals, Bracket B
matches.note: Ended in a little under eight minutes with the Scorpion Deathlock, putting Nemesis into the second round.

matches.stipulation: Greensboro World Cup Quarterfinals, Bracket C
matches.note: Crippler abandoned his usual technical plan and finished with an impact DDT.

matches.stipulation: Greensboro World Cup Quarterfinals, Bracket D
matches.note: Douglas wrestled under his masked "El Volcano" gimmick. Randy Harders appeared on the curtain with a microphone and called Enforcer out over his interference at Showtime; Douglas rolled Enforcer up while he was distracted, winning the bracket.

matches.stipulation: Four Corners Cage Match, elimination rules, two men in the ring at a time
matches.note: Blade pinned TJ Knuckles after a second Guillotine Blade; Mr. X pinned Blade with Cool Moe D holding the legs; Mr. X then clotheslined Cool Moe D and pinned him holding the tights. Afterwards Blade, backed by Dante Inferno, attacked Mr. X in the aisle.

matches.stipulation: Greensboro World Cup Quarterfinals, Bracket C; final match of the first round
matches.note: Flair first won by submission with the Total Elimination and refused to release the hold, then chokeslammed referee Ben Worthington while Poison Ivy laid out Rap Master. The referee staff reversed the decision and awarded the match, and the bracket, to Rap Man by disqualification.

For the CSWA UNITED STATES HEAVYWEIGHT TITLE. Powers seconded by Gina and Susan, Eliminator by Hot Scott. Poison Ivy joined commentary, then left, caned Hot Scott, struck Eliminator's knee and cracked the cane over Powers' head before breaking it over her knee. Referee Patrick Young ruled a double countout, so Powers retained; Eli Flair later told Rudy Seitzer he had overheard talk of a "triangle match" for ELVIS LIVES.

Inferno seconded by Silky Rose; Vizzack wrestled without Sunshine, who was confined at Green Valley. Inferno climbed the turnbuckle with Vizzack on his back in a sleeper and drove both men through a table; Ben Worthington stopped the count and no decision was announced. Inferno then attacked the medics and Steve Radder, and the show went off the air.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "June 2, 1996"

matches.note: Windsor's second CSWA match after losing his debut in Chicago; finished Brigsby with a sleeper hold.
The Sarge billed as returning to the CSWA at 559 lbs after leaving at nearly 600 lbs. First CSWA win for RAGE 'O FIRE.
Both men used chairs; Kaleidoscope finished with a TR sunset flip.
Clark returning after a two-year absence, formerly managed by Sammy "The Mastermind" Benson. Went over 15 minutes; Anarky won with a DDT.
Went the 20 minute time limit. The recap notes Melton had turned down a large offer from Ray S. Cornette.
The 30 minute time limit expired before a pinfall occurred.
Both men were counted out when the action got too heated on the outside; the recap's result line reads "Winner: Countout". No winner is declared.

Pierce came to the ring in street clothes, took the microphone from Rhubarb Jones, announced he was the Unified Champion and would wrestle only Unified Title matches from now on, and refused to wrestle this non-title bout.
Billed as CS EXPRESS vs. MASKED ASSASSINS; the CS Express's first match since returning from Japan. Morton got the cover after a double dropkick while Gibson held off Scope.

ATTAXX billed as the current ASWF World Champion. GUNS escaped the heart punch set-up and stole the win with a small package. After the bell ATTAXX laid GUNS out with a chair as he walked up the aisle; security helped GUNS to the back.

For the Greensboro Heavyweight Championship. Waters won by disqualification when Starr back-dropped him over the top rope, so the belt stayed with Starr. Buckley then announced CS Enterprises had mandated a return match between the two for the Greensboro Title at Battle of the Belts XIV.

matches.stipulation: If Heartbreaker wins, Hornet has said that he'll do whatever the young star wants him to
matches.note: Heartbreaker accompanied by managers Jessica Spencer and Jana Riggny, who tried to interfere with a briefcase; Hornet caught Spencer and escorted her out of the ring. Hornet won with the SCORPION DEATHLOCK after referee Patrick Young checked Heartbreaker's arm three times. Paul Pierce then ran in and beat Heartbreaker senseless while Hornet led the two managers away.

For the United States/National Heavyweight Championship. Hornet walked down to ringside unseen, laid out referee Patrick Young with a forearm, dropkicked Randalls and hit him with Randalls' own Implant DDT, then said something to Reno and left. Reno hit a REVERSE NECKBREAKER and Young recovered to count the three.

For the Enterprise World Championship. Adler never reached the ring. In a filmed segment Adler was pulled over for speeding outside the arena, handcuffed to the door handle of Hornet's limousine and dragged down the street as the limo pulled away. The referee began a ten-count; Windham stopped it at nine and refused a count-out win on the microphone. No result is declared.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "March 11, 1997"

matches.note: For the Enterprise World Championship. Buckley states the match is sanctioned by the CSWA but the title is not — it is owned by CSWA co-owner Chad Merritt exclusively, who hand-picked Michaels as the CSWA's new 'Franchise' and sat at ringside to watch. Michaels finished with a superplex and pinned Worthington with a foot on the chest. Referee not named.

Rematch of a St. Louis meeting in which GUNS' CSWA career was on the line against Dean's mask; Dean is now unmasked. Refereed by Ben Worthington. GUNS caught Dean's crossbody and drove him down on the knee for a modified backbreaker. After the bell GUNS threw Dean into the crowd a second time.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "May 29, 1996"

matches.note: Outlaw's CSWA debut per the recap; finished with a Tombstone Piledriver.
Windsor's CSWA debut. HEAT billed as a former US Heavyweight Champion returning to action.
Master Hakaski revealed The Wizard as his mystery man before the bout.
Justice's CSWA debut; finished with a TR Belly to Belly.

Eliminator was accompanied by Alicia and won with a DDT. The recap opens "Two words: no contest" as a figure of speech for a one-sided beating, then explicitly rules out a no-decision, DQ or count-out and declares a winner.
Mr. Self-Destruct billed as Eli's brother. Reno finished with a swinging neckbreaker.
Heartbreaker billed as AAWC Television Champion, Anarky as the former Greensboro Champion coming off a screwjob loss to Billy Starr. Anarky won with an atomic drop into a quick roll-up.

For the Unified World Tag Team Titles. Billed as DISCO EXPRESS vs. JAPANESE ASSAULT; Japanese Assault managed by Matt Rosenthal. The Disco Express retained with a double booty breaker on Shotgun Shogun. Referee not named in the recap.
For the EN World Tag Team Titles. Billed as <> CUTTERS vs. FIRE & ICE. Endersen finished Cain with a quick DDT.

For the ENTERPRISE WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP. Randalls hit the tombstone piledriver and referee Worthington counted three, and Buckley announced a new champion; Patrick Young then came out, conferred with Worthington, and Worthington ruled that Windham's foot had been on the bottom rope and awarded the belt back to Windham. No winner is declared after the reversal. HORNET and "Golden Boy" Paul Pierce then jumped Randalls and tied a plastic bag around his head until GUNS made the save.

matches.stipulation: Texas Tornado rules, with Teri Melton locked in a steel cage suspended 30 feet above the ring
matches.note: Referee Worthington was knocked down. Teri Melton picked the lock on the suspended cage, dropped 30 feet and hit a Frank'n'Parsons on GUNS; Mitchell covered and Worthington called for the bell, disqualifying Mitchell and Michaels. The winning team was then beaten down anyway as the show went off air.

name: CSWA PRIMETIME in El Paso -- August 7, 1998

date.source: the document's own dateline, "August 7, 1998"

matches.stipulation: special rules: if the match lasted 10 minutes Brigsby would be declared the winner and Hotbody would refund all El Paso
matches.note: Brigsby challenged Hotbody and set the terms. Hotbody charged the ring while Brigsby still had the microphone and finished him inside two minutes with an Inverted DDT, Powerslam and the Spinning Cut.

matches.stipulation: second half of Hotbody's ten-minute two-opponent challenge
matches.note: Worthington stalled at ringside until the referee started counting him out. Hotbody wrestled technically, then hit a diamond cutter and covered with about five seconds left — Parsons says he beat the deadline by two seconds. Parsons puts Hotbody's lifetime record at 14-0 afterwards.

The masked man in tights etched 'EL' came out and threw Hot Scott into the ringside rail while an unknown fan jumped the rail and distracted the referee. The masked man seemed to want the Preacher, but Enforcer charged him and took a metal chair to the head; the Preacher rolled him up and referee Patrick Young counted three.

Ray S. Cornette introduced his team as the EEI Ultimate Tag-Team Champions and declared the bout a non-title affair. Melton got the figure four on Sledgehammer for the submission after about ten minutes.

Watson was missing at the bell and the referee began a standing ten-count; at eight Watson came over the rail from the crowd and dropped Diamond with a loaded closed fist to the back of the head, then yelled for referee Patrick Young to count the pin. Watson threw a roll of quarters into the crowd afterwards.

Douglas was split open after being pulled off the apron, then dropped Michaels throat-first onto the metal railing and climbed back in to beat the ten-count; Michaels was counted out. Douglas needed several stitches to the forehead, Michaels was treated for throat and chest lacerations.

Poison Ivy arrived late with two men and a table, which she covered with broken glass and thumbtacks; Eli clotheslined Powers so both men went over the top and through it. Eli then bench-pressed Powers back into the ring and finished with a Tombstone Piledriver. Referee Ben Worthington did not disqualify them, apparently because the table was outside the ring.

Nemesis worked an STF early; Love answered with a low blow, eye gouges and a slingshot suplex, used Sweet Melissa to distract referee Ben Worthington, and hit a Hurricane Piledriver on the outside before the cover.

For the Unified Tag Team Titles. Elimination Squad is Eliminator and Mysterious, with Hot Scott and later the Rap Master at ringside. Poison Ivy came down with two large men, caned Eliminator twice in the head and had the cane snapped over his knee; Eli then came out of the crowd with a cane of his own and knocked Eliminator over the top, and the two big men brawled on the floor. Guillotine Blade at the thirteen minute mark. Dante Inferno was in Blade's corner under a brown robe; Silky Rose set Katie J's hair on fire and was ejected from ringside. Blade declared over the house mic that "The UnHoly has finished with Hard Body."

Nemesis kayoed referee Patrick Young with a steel chair and Black's Army laid into God's Protege for five minutes until Deacon came to ringside and fought them off. Cool Moe D covered God's Protege as soon as Young recovered.

matches.note: Radder finished with a piledriver.

Billed as three newcomers and as CSWA history; the Eliminator started against Mclarson and never tagged out, taking on both men for nearly 15 minutes. The Deacon came down in a monk outfit to distract him. Eliminator put Crash away with his finisher.

The document's own WINNER line names the Deacon, but the write-up above it says the Deacon was busted open and laid out by the Eliminator with the timekeeper's bell while referee Ben Young was stunned, that Hot Scott took out Deacon's manager the Shepard, and that El Loco covered the fallen Deacon. The two statements contradict each other; the announced result is recorded here.

Doom and the Two Guys made their debut; Disco Express made their redebut. The DiscoMidget returned drunk and was told off by Disco Inferno; while referee Ben Young helped the DiscoMidget to the back a discoball dropped from the roof onto one of the Two Guys.

The printed entrant list repeats "Bloodhunt" and "Chill" twice; they are listed once here. The text calls it 20 of the top stars in the CSWA. Bloodhunt never entered the ring, working over men as they were thrown out. Mark Windham threw GUNS out and was then dropkicked out by Michael Sparks. Boogie Man and Disco Inferno of the Disco Express interfered to eliminate Disco Stu and his partner, and Deacon finished by flinging out Radder and Sparks together.

Main event, roughly 30 minutes, billed as a possible preview for the vacant World Title. No result is given. Mark Windham hit the ring and tore into Troy; Hornet nailed Mark with a Hornet Splash; Mark then crushed Hornet with repeated chair shots; GUNS ran in and cleared both Windhams. The segment ends with GUNS and Hornet staring each other down in the ring.

matches.note: 'WINNER: Tsunami.' Both billed former World Junior Champions; Stokes missed a TR Dropkick.

Beijing Dragon's CSWA debut. 'Beijing Dragon used every trick in his book and more, hooking in vicious submission moves until finally, the referee had to call the match.' The recap's opening 'This one was no contest from the beginning' is a figure of speech; the document declares 'WINNER:  Beijing Dragon'.
CS Express billed as Chad Gibson and Steve Morton; The Destructor works most of the match for Maximum Pain. Finished with the CS Express's double drop kick.
'He finished it off with a figure four leglock to get the submission win.'

No 'WINNER:' line is printed for this match, but the recap states 'it was a DDT and Boston crab that finished Mean Mountain Max off' and that Wright 'will definitely continue to move up the rankings.'
'WINNER: Matthew Waller' - billed as his second win in a row.
'WINNER:  Rodney Lawrence.'
Melton accompanied by Miss Hooters, who stays outside the ring. 'The patented Figure Four Leglock won the match for Melton with a submission by Devil.'
'WINNER:  Mickey Benedict' - step-over-toe hold into a small package.

For the Greensboro Championship. Simmons hit his head on the metal post behind the turnbuckle; 'Dunlap wrapped him up in a cradle to get the three-count and retain his Greensboro Championship after his first title defense.'

'WINNER:  Double DQ.' The referee was knocked out of the ring when Tony Eaton was thrown into him and called for the bell; the brawl carried on until five CSWA officials separated the teams, and CSWA VP Steve Day was hit in the head.

For the EN World Heavyweight Championship. Randalls's legs knocked the referee down; Windham hit the MUPPET MANEUVER off the top with his bungee cord, threw the cord out of the ring and revived the referee for the count. Buckley notes Windham becomes only the second man, with Joey Melton, to hold a singles World Title and a World Tag Team Title at the same time.

For the UNIFIED World Heavyweight Championship. Sanctioned 'by over thirty different leagues as THE official heavyweight championship of the world.' Hornet used the Scorpion Deathlock three times before finishing with a flying body press.

matches.note: Both men came to the ring with chairs; Enforcer accompanied by the entire Elimination Squad. The Rap Man tossed a chair onto the fallen Enforcer, who met Hannibal's dive off the top with it.
Billed as Vizzack's in-ring CSWA debut, with Sunshine at his side; Rap Man accompanied by the Rap Master and the Elimination Squad. Finish was a moonsault.

Douglas, who had announced his own unscheduled debut outside the arena, rushed the ring, worked Road Runner over and 'gets the cover'; no count is described, but Douglas then tells the crowd 'I won this match for each and every one of you' and asks to be entered in the 32-man World Title tournament.
Elite Domination fielded Shawn Diamond and Hannibal. Crippler hooked the neck and leg for the 'Cripple-plex' and got the three-count while HBK2000 blocked Hannibal from breaking up the pin.

Disco Supreme is Disco Stu and Judd Jennrich; the Dirty Duo is Vern Peevler and Bob Stanley. Referee Ben Worthington. Jennrich pressed Peevler overhead and Disco Stu dropkicked him out of Jennrich's arms before the 1-2-3.
The two brawled through the barricade and into the crowd; referee Ben Worthington reached ten and ruled both men counted out. The document's own result line reads 'WINNER: Double Countout'.

Hornet ignored the crowd, told referee Patrick Young to ring the bell and went straight at Worthington. He declined to have his hand raised and instead took the microphone for a long promo aimed at Mark Windham, the Frat, Julius Godreign, Troy Windham, Mike Randalls and GUNS, ending 'that's five.....just 26 more to go through by FISH FUND.'

Elimination Squad fielded Mysterious and Eliminator. The advertised mystery partner turned out to be the returning former Intracontinental Champion Eliminator, brought out of the crowd by Poison Ivy; instead of teaming with Jarvis he dropped him with an implant DDT and left, and Mysterious covered the prone Jarvis. Jarvis was attended to by paramedics and ruled to have a severe concussion, out indefinitely.
Went almost twenty minutes, Crippler cheering God's Protege on from the apron; Love won with a desperation piledriver.

Windham had Brigsby in the sharpshooter when GUNS rushed the ring and deliberately stomped Brigsby in the head. Referee Ben Worthington consulted Patrick Young and, rather than ruling a disqualification, they ruled the match a no-contest; Worthington explained afterwards that GUNS had obviously meant to cost Windham the match.

Minutes after costing Mark Windham his match. Stu would not submit to the bear hug or the Hornet-taught Scorpion deathlock; GUNS pinned him after the bionic knee lift, then gorilla pressed him into the third row.

Troy Windham and members of the Frat attacked Randalls outside the ring and rolled him back in while the referee tended to Starr's turned ankle; Starr, described as unaware of what happened, finished with a Brainbuster.

MAIN EVENT. Moral Majority is Deacon and the Preacher. Radder played possum, chaired the Preacher's right knee behind referee Ben Worthington's back and applied the figure four; the Preacher submitted while Deacon was still fighting Corleone on the floor. The Elimination Squad walked halfway down the aisle to watch.

matches.note: Nevenrose attacked before the bell; Corleone came back with a chicken wing and finished with a superplex from the top.

K-9 started the match before the bell with an elbow off the top and finished with a top rope Frank n' Parsons. After the match the lights went out and a voice Buckley identified as Apocalypse called K-9 to "join your brothers"; K-9 vanished.
Tollens came out in a "Role Model" shirt claiming the gimmick. Tiffany's dropped collection plate was used by Johnson for the finish while referee Patrick Young removed her.

Finished with the Guillotine in just under five minutes. The recap opens "A couple of words could sum this one up: no contest" as a figure of speech about the one-sidedness, not as a ruling; the document then declares Blade the winner.

Radder won by pinfall with the Absolute Zero in just over ten minutes. After the count Apocalypse, Pat Black and Blade bungeed into the cage; K-9 approached from the back; Eddy Love and Kevin Powers made the save.

For the Greensboro Title. Roughly 20 minutes. Harders wrestled with one arm in a sling after a rumored attack by Douglas, and finished by cracking Douglas over the head with a hockey stick he had brought to ringside. Co-Commissioner Chad Merritt watched from the backstage curtain.

For the United States Title. Nemesis won by submission with a Boston Crab after using a chair on Jackson's back while referee Ben Worthington was down. He refused to release the hold until VP of Security Gregg Gethard threatened him with suspension.

For the CSWA World Championship. Main event. Hornet sprang from the rafters on a harness and cracked Vizzack over the head with a plate of glass; Love and Sweet Melissa left. No finish and no ruling. Afterward Vizzack threw the World Title belt to Hornet and promised to reclaim it at Battle of the Belts.

matches.note: Hotbody, billed as undefeated at 18-0, ran through Wright with clotheslines, a press slam, a spinebuster slam and a suicide dive to the floor. On Ray S. Cornette's advice Wright did not return to the ring and referee Patrick Young called the countout; Randall Jaminson then came out and Hotbody left through the crowd.
Described as having taken place before the broadcast. Enforcer attacked before the opening bell, hit a DDT and an elbow drop and took the three count.
Described as the other dark match of the evening. Sledgehammer and Chainsaw were off their game with poor tags and bad timing and the Elimination Squad took the victory.

Rap Man's manager the Rap Master got involved every time the referee turned his back; Sparks rallied and pinned Rap Man after a hard-hitting Piledriver. Billed as Sparks's first appearance since his Fish Fund loss.
Described as already having taken place; Ego Buster was defeated quickly and swiftly despite a considerable size advantage.
Jaminson attacked HBK2000 before the bell and took the beating outside the ring; referee Patrick Young disqualified him and awarded the victory to HBK2000, who may need stitches.

Apocalypse won at the eleven-minute mark with a pair of inverted DDTs. His partner Pat Black, at ringside, came in afterwards and looked almost sorry for God's Protege, raising the question of a recruitment into Black's Army. Apocalypse's second tournament win.
Called the final Greensboro match of the night and worked live. Nemesis shook Mysterious off the top rope groin-first and finished with a Belly to Belly Superplex.

matches.stipulation: TOP CONTENDERS MATCH for the CSWA World Championship
matches.note: The two were named as candidates by President Merritt with Hornet injured and Starr missing in action. Referee Worthington waved off an apparent three count on a piledriver, ruling Radder got his hand up; Vizzack then hit a Moonsault for the win and the top-contender status.

For the United States Title. Powers led out by Gina and Susan. Powers used Gina as a shield outside, Susan hit the Preacher with her purse and kicked him from behind so Powers could lay him out with the ring bell, and finally Powers hit a low blow behind the referee's back followed by a Stunner for the pin. Buckley calls it a win 'in a disgusting manner'.

matches.stipulation: one fall contest with a one hour time limit
matches.note: For the CSWA WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP. MAIN EVENT. Melton led out by Ray S. Cornette, Love by Sweet Melissa; Kevin Powers, Gina and Susan sat in the front row, Powers telling Rudy Seitzer he was there to make sure nothing funny happened. Melton controlled much of it and hit a Front Layout Superplex. matches.note: Damien Xeno came to ringside and shot a jet of flame from his sleeve at Wells on the top rope; Deacon hit the Altar Call for the three count and was booed out of the building. Wells was taken for treatment.
Debut for the 327-pound "Malice Man", who finished with his camel clutch variant, the "Whiskey Bent and Hell Bound". Brigsby is described as a former US Tag Champ.
Wylde's return to a CSWA ring after a long absence; finished with The Wildcard Splash. He celebrated by jumping into ring announcer Rhubarb Jones' arms.

HaVoC's debut. He doused Pyro with the contents of a can taken from under the ring and finished with "the H-Bomb", a spinning powerbomb, counted by referee Patrick Young. Afterward he poured gasoline over Pyro and lit a match before security restrained him.

Battle of debuting stars. "The English Gent" Lawrence Stanley came to ringside and propositioned Gettis' manager Helen; while Gettis was distracted Desmond hit an iron butterfly suplex and rolled him up for the three.

Stanley debuting with his manservant Lord Alfred, who tossed in a steel cane. Stanley used it below the belt and finished with his Guillotine DDT off the top. Called an upset over the co-leader of the Unholy.
X-Rated with manager and valet Desire; roughly fifteen minutes before a jawbreaker escape and a five-star frogsplash gave him his first CSWA win.

The Hooded Falcon attacked from above with a staff, was knocked out by a double clothesline, then played possum and caned Solomon in the back of the head as he set up the Crucifier, letting Wicked Sight roll over for the pin. Referee Ben Worthington officiating.

For the UNIFIED TAG TEAM TITLES. Eddy Love arrived late; Patrick Young started a standing ten count and Kevin Powers wrestled alone for much of the match. Love eventually knocked out Ben Worthington and then Crippler with a hidden object, Sweet Melissa kicked Jackson, and backup referee Manuel Juarez counted Powers' pin on Crippler.

Vizzack wrestled with his right shoulder taped after a masked man attacked him backstage with a lead pipe. Referee Manuel Juarez counted the fall on a reversal in which Buckley says Dexter clearly had the tights. Dexter accompanied by Sugar Blossom.

The arena lights went out; when they returned Blade was gone. A steel cage lowered around Cool Moe D and a cloaked "mystery man" - identified by Buckley as Rick Codine, introduced by a voiceover as GENOCIDE - beat him with a black bat. No finish and no ruling.

matches.stipulation: no-disqualification match (proposed by Hornet from the aisle and accepted by Apocalypse)
matches.note: Billed as Apocalypse vs. Aaron Douglas' Mystery Opponent; Douglas revealed Hornet by video wall from a private plane. Billy Starr came out from under the ring with a chair; Miso tripped Hornet; Pat Black and Randy Harders came out. Hornet and Starr left up the aisle and referee Patrick Young ruled a count-out win for Apocalypse, who had been promised the right to name Douglas' next title challenger.

matches.stipulation: Hotbody promised to beat his opponent in under five minutes or personally refund every ticket price, then added that if
matches.note: Hotbody attacked Brigsby on the floor before the bell and had Rhubarb Jones call out the countdown. Brigsby tapped to a Dragon Sleeper with at least a minute and a half left.
Shown as part of the pre-broadcast block. Crippler made Spanky submit to a figure four leg lock after about five minutes.
Pre-broadcast block. Timmy scored a quick pin, described as won in under one minute.

Pre-broadcast block. Starr demanded a CORPORATION member as a partner and Eddy Love answered, debuting as a Corporation member. At the six-minute mark Love gave Ron Marshall an implant DDT and Starr followed with a Shooting Starr Press.

Pre-broadcast block. ARROGANCE is Joey Melton and Peyton Wright; the Moral Majority is the Preacher and Deacon. As Deacon looked set to pin Peyton Wright, Randall Jaminson nailed the back of his knee with Ray Cornette's tennis racket; Wright tagged Melton, who put the figure four on the injured knee and Deacon tapped out. The Preacher looked upset with his partner for submitting.
Apocalypse finished with a Tombstone Piledriver. Afterwards his 'new ally' Pat Black threw in a chair; Apocalypse chaired the bleeding Ego Buster and the two gave him a DDT on the chair.
Ten minutes in, Jaminson left the ring, returned with a chair and hit Nemesis in the head three consecutive times; the referee disqualified him. The document notes Nemesis is now 1-0 in his bracket.
Described as an easy win for God's Protege, who decimated Stu.

HBK2000 had just taken the contracted five-minute beating from Elite Domination alongside the Crippler, immediately before this tournament match; Buckley calls it unfair. Mysterious won with a Dragon Suplex at the six-minute mark.

For the Unified World Tag-Team Championship. MAIN EVENT and the champions' first defence. Destruction Crew is Chainsaw and Sledgehammer, billed as former MHW Champions. Boogie Man chaired Chainsaw on the floor, and Disco Inferno finished with a Flying Guillotine Leg Drop off the top.

Stanley released an arm bar and followed with a small package for three, possibly with help from Lord Alfred earlier in the match. Word came later that Wolfstein suffered a separated shoulder and would be out several weeks. Stanley beat him with a chair afterwards until referees restrained him.

name: CSWA SHOWTIME at the MEADOWLANDS

date.source: the document's own dateline, "January 17, 1996"

matches.note: Fan-voted card; Buckley calls this the most requested match. Teri Melton seconded Steven Flair and interfered with a superkick and a chair. Mike Flair, a member of the Horsemen, is billed as CSWA Presidential champion and Steven Flair as former Unified champion. Referee Troutman. Mike Flair pinned him with the figure four while Steven was out from an outside DDT.

Also billed as the most requested match; former Unified World Tag Team Champions and current tag partners in the Dream Team. Before the bell the Wild Asian and Bandit ambushed Taylor and put him through a table while Michaels watched. Mickey Van Buren led Taylor out later. Teri Melton slipped Taylor brass knuckles, he refused to use them on Michaels and levelled her with them instead, and Michaels clipped his knee and rolled him up. Buckley says Taylor had a hand on the bottom rope and the pin should not have counted. Referee Ben Worthington.

Melton pinned Karelin after flipping him head-first into the turnbuckle by the tights, with Benson saying he had a handful of tights. Both men are billed as former Corporation members now feuding with Ray S. and his men.

Assigned referee Manuel Juarez let a table-and-weapons brawl run unchecked, with Johnny Tropic bringing in two tables and a branding iron to help Williams. Senior referee Ben Worthington came out and called for the bell when Randalls produced a steel rod; Buckley calls the result a Double DQ. Randalls then double-arm-powerbombed Worthington. No winner declared.

matches.stipulation: Disco Express w/Disco Midget vs <> Cutters w/Red Midget; if one midget is tagged in the other must come in for the other
matches.note: Main event. The <> Cutters are billed as EN World Tag Team Champions and are said to be furious at being teamed with a midget. Commentator Sammy Benson left the booth, pulled the Red Midget off the apron, sent him into the ringpost and DDT'd him in the ring, letting the legal Disco Midget cover. The Red Midget then clipped Benson's knee to close the show.

Patrick Young refereed.

For the GREENSBORO HEAVYWEIGHT Title. Anarky was accompanied by Poison IVY. Starr had Anarky in the STF for minutes; IVY climbed the apron, kissed Starr, then drove her knee into his groin through the second rope, and Anarky rolled him up with a handful of tights.
Billed as a fan-requested DREAM MATCH, "a war of the Mitchells". Frankie put Todd through the broadcast table on the outside; Todd finished with a POWERBOMB.

Bailey was accompanied by Maxwell Diamond and the FIRM, who interfered repeatedly. Jasmine of the FIRM slipped Bailey a lead ball; HORNET intercepted it, hit Bailey with it and covered, but referee Patrick Young saw the weapon and awarded the match to Bailey by disqualification.

HORNET and Mark Windham are billed as America's Team, reuniting after nearly three years. "The Golden Boy" Paul Pierce ran in and broke an axe handle over Mike Randalls' back and cracked the other half over GUNS' head; HORNET pulled referee Patrick Young out of the ring while Windham applied the TORTURE RACK. Young returned, lifted GUNS' arm three times and called for the bell.

Announced as not for the UNIFIED Title. Pierce pulled handcuffs from his boot and cuffed Adler's hands behind his back; America's Team ran in and beat Adler with the axe handle while Pierce applied the MASTERLOCK. The broadcast ran out of time with the <> Cutters hitting the ring; no finish is given in this copy.

Billed as a return encounter after the two met in Nashville with nothing settled; Sparks finished with a Tombstone Piledriver.

Buckley bills it as a bout 'sanctioned by the CSWA as a top contenders bout'. Deacon accompanied by the Shepherd (and referred to as managed by the Preacher); Eliminator accompanied by his manager Hot Scott. Finish was the 'razor's edge' powerbomb Deacon calls the Alter Call.

Eli's partner is billed only as the Mystery Partner / Masked Man and is never identified in this copy. Silver removed the top turnbuckle pad; Eli was whipped into the exposed steel and rolled up with a school-boy. Afterward the masked man caned Silver, Hell's Caretaker slapped Poison Ivy unconscious, and Eli caned the Caretaker and powerbombed Silver.

Loser was to be the winner's servant for a day. Nathan Storm splashed Randalls off the top while he had the Devastator locked in, so Randalls won by disqualification and the servant clause did not take effect. The <> Cutters and Maxwell Diamond then beat Randalls down; Tsunami and Wildstar ran out to save him.

For the EN WORLD TAG-TEAM CHAMPIONSHIP. Billed as The <> CUTTERS (C) with Maxwell Diamond vs THE ARMED FORCES with TTL and Ray S. Cornette; the Armed Forces' US Tag titles were not at stake. Referee Ben Worthington was knocked down; Cornette interfered with a tennis racket; co-Commissioner Chad Merritt entered to stop the match and accidentally clocked Submarine with his cell phone, then counted the fall himself. Buckley is not certain the result stands.

Originally signed as GUNS/Karelin/Melton vs the Corporation trio; Joey Melton left the arena after taking Cornette's money, and Hornet took his place while GUNS sat out to prepare for the main event, making it two on three. Eliminations: Karelin pinned Peyton Wright after a German suplex; Williams pinned Karelin after Cyborgus hit him with the metal arm; Hornet pinned Cyborgus after GUNS ran in with a chair; Williams was then counted out.

For the EN WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP. GUNS defending. After GUNS hit the Bionic Kneelift and broke the cover to confront Submarine at ringside, the Armed Forces pulled him out and TTL handcuffed him to the ring railings; Worthington counted him out. Viper wins by countout; no title change stated. GUNS was then beaten with chairs and hit with the ring bell, and Jim Williams brought the branding iron out before Karelin made the save.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "February 14, 1999"

matches.note: Given as 18:36. Blade ripped off Deacon's shirt, exposing an enormous cross branded on his back, and Buckley noted The Shepherd's hands were bandaged. Deacon kicked out of the Guillotine Blade and finished with the ALTAR CALL.

matches.note: Lunacy countered a back bodydrop into a DDT for the pin.

Pain and Hurt are the Masters of Misery. Brigsby and Paige collided head to head coming off the top rope and Pain pinned both men at once with a foot on each; both were stretchered out and sent to hospital.
Billed as Matthew Lewis' CSWA debut; managed by Kevin Sykora, he finished with a back-superplex.
Before the bell Steel Viper tipped Kaledioscope off his stretcher and Viperbombed him on the concrete; he won with the Vipersault and then kept attacking both men afterwards.
Mike Day and Kamikaze are the Electric Express. Matt Rosenthal's two unnamed masked men jumped them on the way to the ring and won with a double powerbomb on Day.
The Wild Asian came to ringside with Bandit and finished with a Northern Lights Suplex.
Called a big upset; the Ringmaster rolled Bonecrusher up after a missed corner elbow. Referee Patrick Young. Announcers note the Ringmaster had yet to lose in CSWA competition.
Billed as the CSWA debut of both men. Starr won with a bridging dragon suplex, which the announcers said they had seen from someone before but could not place.

The Disco Express are the Disco Inferno and the Boogie Man, accompanied by the Disco Midget; the Masked Assassins are Scope and Bullet, called former Unified World Tag Team Champions. Finish was the Discobomb.

For the GREENSBORO Championship. Billed as the final rematch: if Bandit did not win the title he could get no further shot. With Praxis fading in the Bow and Arrow his manager Dr. Guggen entered and kicked Bandit, and Ben Worthington disqualified Praxis. Bandit took the win but not the belt, so Bob Praxis is still Greensboro Champion. The Wild Asian then dropkicked Guggen into the guano wheelbarrow.

NC-17 are Tsunami and Wildstar, seconded by Ray S. Cornette; the CS Express are Chad Gibson and Steve Morton. The United States Tag Team Championship belts were not on the line. Gibson countered a snatch powerbomb into a bridging Frank-N-Parsons.

For the USN CHAMPIONSHIP. Michaels' first defence since taking the United States/National Championship from Timmy Windham at the X-Mas Spectacular; Karelin was seconded by Mad Mike. Michaels blocked a German suplex and hooked a cradle. Afterwards Karelin shook Michaels' hand and raised it.

The Eliminator's INTRACONTINENTAL Championship was expressly not on the line. Alicia and Poison Ivy were at ringside for Eli; referee Patrick Young. Finish was a powerbomb, after which the lights went black, Prizm vanished from the ring and Dr. Silver appeared on the video wall.

For the EN WORLD TAG TEAM CHAMPIONSHIP. Ern Enderson and Tully Planchard, managed by Maxwell Diamond, against Battleship and Submarine, seconded by TTL. With Diamond on the apron and Worthington arguing with him, Battleship hit the referee coming off the ropes; Worthington called a disqualification. Buckley says the Cutters win via DQ and keep the belts because of Diamond's interference, and that Battleship would otherwise have had the three count.

matches.stipulation: SIX-MAN TAG TEAM MATCH in a ROOFED CAGE
matches.note: For the UNIFIED World Tag Team Championship. Conditional stipulations: if Mike Flair were pinned by Matthews, Taylor or Michaels they would become Presidential Champion; if Taylor or Michaels were pinned by Chain or Samson, Chain and Samson would become Unified World Tag Team Champions. Michaels' USN title was not on the line. Teri Melton came down and threw Lex Taylor brass knuckles; Flair stomped his hand, took them and decked Taylor. matches.stipulation: STEEL CAGE SUBMISSION MATCH, LOSER LEAVES FOR SIXTY DAYS
matches.note: Roofed cage, so Teri Melton could not interfere; no pinfalls, only submission or three arm drops. Ran roughly thirty-five minutes. Melton tied Flair's arms with the tag rope, hung him from the top rope and applied the figure four until Flair submitted; Flair is gone from the CSWA for sixty days. Teri Melton walked out on Flair afterwards.

matches.stipulation: EN WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP TRIANGLE MATCH, no disqualifications, no count-outs; champion Randalls enters fifteen minutes in
matches.note: For the EN WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP. GUNS and Windham started; Randalls entered on the horn at fifteen minutes. GUNS small-packaged Windham to eliminate him, with Randalls declining to break the count, then caught a flying bodypress and powerslammed Randalls for his second EN World Championship.

For the UNIFIED World Heavyweight Championship. Sixty-minute limit, one fall. Hornet came out taped around the torso and back after GUNS accidentally hit him with the EN belt, beating Worthington's ten count; under CSWA rules the title would have gone to Williams had he been unable to compete. Johnny Tropic interfered twice and Worthington called for the bell when Tropic hit Hornet with a metal rod, giving Hornet the win by disqualification and the title. Billed as a rematch, Platoon having won the first meeting. Eliminator hit no offensive move until the small package that won it; the announcers put it down to Alicia being in hospital after a near-fatal car crash.
Submission to the THUNDER DEATHLOCK; the write-up says Smolowitz quit to save his legs for the ULTRATITLE tournament.
Billed as PYROMANIA vs MASKED ASSASINS. Smoke pulled Scope out of the ring so that Flame landed on Bullet, and Flame hooked the legs and tights for the three.

Guns managed by TTL, Eskimo Joe by Don Ho. Don Ho distracted the referee and Joe pulled a chain, but missed. The finish is shown only as an instant replay of this match, not announced by the ring announcer: Guns took a sunset flip with a handful of tights.

For the CSWA UNITED STATES/NATIONAL HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP. Champion retained. With the referee down, Miss Hooters entered, dropkicked Dunlap off the top rope, splashed him on the floor and rolled him back in for the cover. Dunlap is billed as the challenger and as GREENSBORO CHAMPION.

For the UNIFIED WORLD TAG TEAM CHAMPIONSHIPS. Full Force win by disqualification; the document does not say the belts changed hands. Muppet Mania attacked during Rhubarb Jones' introductions by swinging in on bungee cords from the rafters, and Pestillence and Beijing Dragon of the Suicide Squad then ran in on Full Force.

For the ENTERPRISE WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP. Champion retained; 60 minute time limit. Tsunami accompanied by Johnny V, whom Randalls clotheslined off the apron and later piledrove on the concrete. Both men bladed heavily; weapons included a broken wooden chair leg, camera equipment and a piece of shattered lens glass. Johnny V threw the EN title belt in and Randalls DDT'd Tsunami on it for the win.
Joined in progress at 31:13. A masked man walked down, chaired Windham while he had the Sharpshooter on, and Bonecrusher covered. Buckley chased the masked man to the locker room for an interview.

matches.note: Chad Merritt watched from the front row. Michaels played possum in the corner, then hit a SHOOTING STAR PRESS; Ben Worthington counted the three.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round
matches.note: Barton is signed to a CSWL contract. Erotic Robin took cheap shots for Massacre, who finished the job with a 2x4 after nearly 12 minutes.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round
matches.note: Ben Worthington was knocked down by an elbow from Pestilence; Xavier Virile came down and decked Hotbody with a frying pan, and Pestilence rolled him over for the three.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round
matches.note: Tsunami missed a reverse moonsault and Starr rolled clear and hooked the legs for the three.
