matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round
matches.note: Wildstar scored a three-count after putting Jackson through a table set up by Jimmy V., but kept going — superplexing Jackson through a second table and setting up a piledriver — and referee Worthington called for the bell and reversed the decision, awarding the match and the second-round spot to Eric Jackson.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round
matches.note: Payne finished with a maneuver almost like a mafia kick for the quick three-count.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round
matches.note: Greco billed as a member of "The Family", the newest stable in the CSWA; Masked Man #1 as one of the men who apparently either has a grudge against GUNS or an alliance with America's Team. Greco won with a DDT.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round
matches.note: Windham won by submission with the Sharpshooter. The recap opens by playing on the phrase 'no contest' as an idiom for a one-sided match, not as a ruling.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round
matches.note: GUNS, at ringside with Bonecrusher, jumped on the apron and nailed Martinez with the time keeper's bell, then held Troy's feet down for the pin. Buckley explains GUNS was helping out a fellow jWo member.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round
matches.note: Mahler billed as a former seven-time SSW World Champ. The masked man reversed position in midair off Mahler's top rope backdrop and hooked the leg.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round
matches.note: Both men came to the ring together led by "Hardcore" Jimmy V., both being part of DAWN of a NEW DAY. They laughed off the lock-up, Junior Hornet lay down on the mat, and Troy covered him; a confused Ben Worthington counted three. Buckley calls it a disgrace.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round
matches.note: Nardoni is the second member of The Family in action. Meloneer, billed both as RF Meloneer and Rocky Ford Meloneer and described as the latest Greensboro Champion before Merritt stripped him, finished with the Cantaloupe Crush. Ben Worthington refereed.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round
matches.note: Rocco Nardini and Vito Greco bolted down the aisle and attacked Virile to protect "The Boss" of The Family, giving Virile the disqualification win.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, First Round
matches.note: Timmy Windham used "The Clear" and the Kermy Kick, and finished with the Fozzie Flip, his version of the Frank n' Parsons.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, Second Round
matches.note: Chad Merritt came to the ring with Michaels and cut a promo calling him a god and demanding the crowd bow down; as Merritt walked out and Michaels turned around, Massacre rolled him up for the three. Buckley calls it an upset of galactic proportions.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, Second Round
matches.note: Famine, with NGEN President Paul Miller, ambushed Pestilence on his way to the ring and clotheslined and wailed on him; referee Troutman counted him out. Starr left the ring rather than take part. Miller then cut a promo on Starr and on the CSWA, and Famine turned on Miller, belting him in the mouth and hitting a spinning piledriver.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, Second Round
matches.note: Held during a commercial break and reported afterwards: Greco won "in about eight seconds after a vicious chokeslam".

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, Second Round
matches.note: Joined in progress 6:38 in. Jimmy V. put Troy's foot on the ropes and held the referee; Junior Hornet ran in and was piledriven; Mark Windham came down, knocked Jimmy V. out with a chair, and then, aiming at Troy, caught the Masked Man with the chair when Troy reversed the whip. Troy hit THE SLACKKNIFE for the three.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, Second Round
matches.note: Both men went through tables. Windham knocked out referee Pee Wee Troutman on a rebound. Masked Man #2 came in with a chair and a microphone, laid Bonecrusher out, then powerbombed Windham off the top rope, unmasked as HEAT, spat on Windham, rolled Bonecrusher on top of him and dragged Troutman over to count the three.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, Second Round
matches.note: GUNS entered on a bye. Bonecrusher came to the apron, Meloneer grabbed him by the collar, and Bonecrusher dropped a pair of brass knuckles that GUNS picked up unseen by the referee; GUNS clobbered Meloneer for the three. Mark Windham then ran out and crowned Bonecrusher with a chair.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, Second Round
matches.note: Mark Windham attacked his brother Timmy backstage before the match — slamming a wooden bench over his head in front of their father Alan Windham — and Timmy was taken to hospital. Buckley reports the win was awarded to Virile, who will meet GUNS at the next card.

matches.note: Michaels kept Watson on the mat with suplexes and finished with a tombstone piledriver.

Hotbody, a surprise guest, offered an open challenge from the ring and Spanky Richards reluctantly answered. Hotbody ended it in under two minutes with his 'Spining Cut' Airplane Spin/Diamond Cutter for his first CSWA win, then kissed a woman at ringside.
See-saw for ten minutes; Douglas ended it with a Piledriver and a three count.

matches.stipulation: the loser will be forced at our next card and in humble form offer apologies and praise to the victors AND on top of it
matches.note: Elite Domination is Page Michaels and the wrestler formerly known as Da Crack Baby; Degeneration Next is The Crippler and HBK2000. Michaels pinned the Crippler with a Diamond Cutter.
Eli Flair, led to the ring by Poison Ivy after his first-round tournament loss, finished with a Running Powerslam at about six minutes; Ivy raised his hand in the ring.

A short intermission was held while the cage was assembled. Both men bled heavily; Mysterious dropkicked Diamond off the top rope while Diamond was leaning face-first on the steel and scored the three count.

For the Unified World Tag-Team Championship. SWAT Team is Colt and Beretta; Disco Express is Boogie Man and Disco Inferno, with the Disco Midget. The Disco Midget bit Colt's hand on the ropes and then baited Beretta out of the corner, where Disco Inferno chaired him in the face; Boogie Man then re-applied the figure four and Colt tapped out. Referee Ben Worthington.

Hornet came to the ring first to collect on the Dallas stipulation and introduced the renamed wrestler as NEMESIS, then stayed at ringside coaching him. Nemesis won by submission with the Scorpion Deathlock.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, SECOND ROUND

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, SECOND ROUND
matches.note: The masked man with 'E.L' stamped on his tights swung a chair at the Preacher and hit Windham instead; Windham recovered, superplexed the Preacher off the top and finished with an implant DDT.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, SECOND ROUND
matches.note: Eliminator played possum on the bionic knee, then clotheslined GUNS over the top; after a back body drop and a ring-post shot on the floor Eliminator rolled in and GUNS was counted out. Teri Melton on commentary calls a countout victory 'at best weak'.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, SECOND ROUND
matches.note: Joey Melton ran down looking for revenge from round one and was held back by security and the referee; while the referee was distracted, Peyton Wright came out of the audience on the far side and laid Godreign out with a steel chair, leaving Sparks an easy three count.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, SECOND ROUND
matches.note: Teri Melton left the booth to be at ringside as Starr's manager. Godreign considered interfering for the Frat but was stopped by Randall Jaminson of the Corporation, who had placed members incognito around ringside; Starr rolled Windham up while he was watching Godreign get escorted away.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, SECOND ROUND
matches.note: Deacon accompanied by the Shepherd. Eddy Love came out to the announce position to plug a 'Sammy Benson Defense Fund' while the masked man with E.L. on his tights chaired both Deacon and Vizzack and placed Vizzack on top — Buckley concludes Love and the masked man are partners. Later Aaron Douglas jumped out of the crowd, clotheslined the Shepherd and hit Deacon with the Shepherd's metal crook; Vizzack then hit a Tornado DDT from the top rope for the pin. Referee Ben Worthington.

Teri Melton at ringside for Starr; she yanked Sunshine off the apron and screamed at her until she ran off, which the commentators say cost Vizzack his focus. Starr won by submission with the STF after clipping the knee.
The document notes this one was written 'in short form' due to a lack of roleplay. Sparks gained the submission with a Step-Over-Toe-Hold after Eliminator's knee hit the middle turnbuckle.

Sweet Melissa repeatedly interfered — unhooking the figure four, a chair shot on the floor, tackling referee Ben Worthington — and Love finally blasted Windham with a black loaded glove pulled from his tights before a backslide got the three count.

Billed as the main event and the final match in Bracket #1. Black worked the back with a cross face chicken wing; Hornet came back with a Shooting Star Press and won by tap-out to the Scorpion Deathlock.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "July 8, 1998"

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: Side stipulation: if Da Crack Baby won, Hornet would join Elite Domination; if Hornet won, Da Crack Baby would change his name to whatever Hornet chose. Hornet won by submission with the Scorpion, then helped the young man out of the ring.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: Billed as the rubber match between tag partners, their series standing at a win apiece. Radder finished with the Frostbite powerbomb.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: Rap Man worked with the Rapmaster yelling instructions; God's Protege took it with a shortarm clothesline, snap suplex and an elbow smash from the top.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: Called 'the biggest upset so far in the tournament' and Black's first CSWA match. Randalls squashed referee Ben Worthington in the corner and attacked Black with a chair; Hornet ran down and chaired Randalls, and Black's valet Lady Death rolled Black on top and revived Worthington.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: Michaels got three early pin attempts and reached the ropes to escape the crossface chicken wing; GUNS needed a final bionic kneelift.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: Eliminator won with his patented leglock.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: Referee Patrick Young left the ring trying to stop Sparks using the ringside rail; Sparks dropped the Ego Buster throat-first over the rail anyway, then dragged him in for the one-two-three.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: Jennrich is described as still seeking a match with Co-Commissioner Chad Merritt; Godreign, the former CSWA US Champion who gave up his front-office post for the Frat, won with the Reign of God leglock.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: Billed as the first match of Bracket Two. Love ended it with a piledriver after eight minutes.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: Winner was guaranteed to face Eddy Love, assuring a rookie a place in the quarter-finals. A missed headbutt off the top let Powers put Crippler out with a second sleeper.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: Bottom half of Bracket Two. An errant clothesline put the referee down; a masked man with the initials 'E.L' on his tights hit the ring with a chair, apparently aiming for the Preacher, and blasted the Enforcer instead. The Preacher finished from there.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: Mostly fought outside the ring; an implant DDT after six minutes ended it.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: Billed as Eli Flair's return to the CSWA after over a year away; he is described as never having been beaten for the IC title, which he held longer than any other man. Past twenty minutes Deacon recovered and hit his finisher.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: The referee took a bump and could not continue, so Co-Commissioner Stephen Thomas came in to call the rest of the match. Three men in suits served Thomas and Merritt with papers — a summons to appear in court, apparently a lawsuit Douglas filed against Merritt and Thomas — and Douglas nodded and winked at them. Douglas went to crack a vodka bottle over the head of the 'Sunshine' he had brought out (a drunken Disco Midget in a wig), she ducked and hit him with a right hand, and Vizzack rolled him up.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: Third match of Bracket Four and Apocalypse's debut. With Apocalypse about to finish Starr, the Ego Buster rushed in and put a chair into Starr's back; the document calls the result an automatic DQ and Starr moves on.

matches.stipulation: CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP TOURNAMENT, FIRST ROUND
matches.note: Melton had the figure four set up when Julius Godreign hit the ring trying to send referee Ben Worthington away; while the two argued outside, the Bandit took Melton out with a trash can, and Worthington re-entered to count the pin. The document calls it 'a win he didn't deserve'.

name: CSWA SUPERPRIMETIME in Decatur: Christmas At Ground Zero

date.source: the document's own dateline, "December 24, 1995"

matches.note: Debut of the masked Mega Force, managed by Mr. Saki. Won by submission to the Scorpion Deathlock; Mega Force refused to release the hold until Saki entered the ring.
Billed as a debut for Matthews, who is seconded by Mickey Van Buren. Finish was a sunset flip off the top rope.
Billed in the match header as THE FORCE vs. THE MAGNIFICENT MARVELS; the commentary names the members. The Force are managed by Mr. Saki. Ultra Force pinned Tranzor after a superbomb.
Billed as the Ringmaster's debut.
Billed as Lunacy's CSWA debut. El Magnifique won with a jump splash off the top.
Devastator won with a powerbomb.

Commentator Sammy Benson was ordered into the match by Co-Commissioners Chad Merritt and Stephen Thomas. The match turned into a ringside brawl with roughly ten wrestlers acting as impromptu lumberjacks. Ivy won after a low blow.
Chain won with the Lethal Injection. Jimmy Ray Vaughn interfered on Chain's behalf; Ivan's own manager Mad Mike sat on commentary and declined to help him.
Wild Asian won by bridging back out of a sunset flip attempt.
Michaels, bleeding from the right eye, won with a superkick followed by the Heartbreaker. Lex Taylor was in his corner.

Played as a comedy match in which both men repeatedly injured themselves. Referee Ben Worthington counted both men down on the floor for ten. Both were stretchered out and reported taken to a local hospital.

For the GREENSBORO CHAMPIONSHIP. Billed as GREENSBORO CHAMPIONSHIP RE-MATCH. Praxis retained after Dr. Guggen exposed a turnbuckle; Praxis reversed a whip into it and hit the Guano Drop. Bandit demanded the match be restarted; Worthington refused. Earlier in the match Praxis shoved commentator Mad Mike into a wheelbarrow of manure.

matches.stipulation: 20 MAN, OVER THE TOP ROPE BATTLE ROYAL
matches.note: For the PRESIDENTIAL CHAMPIONSHIP. For the Presidential Championship vacated by Jim Williams. The advertised field named CARL BRIGSBY, but he and Wesley Paige were reported hospitalised after their match and Henderson Bramble was substituted in. Sammy Flair eliminated himself in order to eliminate Vince Bailey; Bob Praxis pulled Bandit out from the floor after his own elimination. Flair eliminated the Wild Asian last.

Flair flattened Karelin with brass knuckles passed through the cage by Ray S. Cornette and threw them away before the referee revived; Joey Melton then reached through the cage and placed Karelin's foot on the rope to break the count. Karelin won with a Russian Sickle and a German suplex. Mad Mike appeared in Karelin's corner, leaving the Corporation.

Thirty-minute time limit. GUNS scored a three count with the Bionic knee-lift, but ring announcer Rhubarb Jones declared the bell had sounded first and announced a time-limit draw. Afterwards Windham clipped GUNS' knee and applied the Scorpion Deathlock until Hornet made the save.

appearances.source: the fed's own served card for this show, which bills the match

date.source: the document's own dateline, "March 23, 1997"

matches.note: Hellion's CSWA debut; billed as having recently beaten ATTAXX for the EFW World Title, as WWX Television Champion and current Tri-State Champion. Finished with "The Wake-Up Call" off the top.
Spunkmeyer showered the fans with muffins on his entrance, one of which hit Sammy Benson between the eyes; finished Paige with a modified neckbreaker.
Stokes billed as former PRODIGY Lightweight Champ, back from three years in Japan. Wolf won with the powerbomb at the 10:50 mark; no "WINNER:" line is printed.
Eliminator returning from a knee injury, accompanied by Poison IVY, who caned Tidal Wave while Eli distracted referee Pee Troutman. Eli won by submission with THE ELIMINATOR.
Southern hit a POWERBOMB, flipped over, hooked the legs and bridged for the three.

Billed as KILLER INSTINCT vs. the Jenkins World Order. Rhubarb Jones announced that GUNS would not participate due to his recent incarceration and family trauma, and Bonecrusher chose to wrestle it as a handicap match. Referee Ben Worthington was knocked down; BATTLESHIP and SUBMARINE — the ARMED FORCES, banned from the CSWA — climbed the rail, attacked Killer Instinct, then turned on Bonecrusher, catapulting him over the top into the security railing. Buckley reports the ruling: Killer Instinct win by disqualification.

Not contested. CSWA Vice-President Gregg Gethard announced backstage to Rudy Seitzer that Bonecrusher, taken away by ambulance after the Armed Forces attack, could not compete and that Troy Windham would win by count-out, becoming the first member of the FINAL FOUR without stepping in the ring.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Tournament Third Round
matches.note: Refereed by Patrick Young. Massacre worked Starr's surgically weak neck with a long reverse chinlock, kicked out of a string of near falls and finally caught Starr's flying body press into a POWER SLAM for the three.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Championship Tournament Third Round
matches.note: Refereed by Patrick Young. The masked man used an abdominal stretch and a step-over-toe hold and finished with a running clothesline, sending himself and Joe Massacre into the semifinals.

GUNS appeared after all, having missed the earlier tag match. Virile jumped him while ref Ben Worthington checked GUNS' boots. GUNS finished with a top rope belly to belly and then a powerbomb off the top rope, and walked out without celebrating.

matches.stipulation: NO DQ, NO COUNTOUT, PINFALLS COUNT EVERYWHERE
matches.note: A brawl through the concourse: chairs, a broom, a storage room, a concession stand, a mustard tub, a popcorn machine and a hotdog grill. Randalls got a two-count behind the counter. Teri Melton — unseen in the CSWA since late the previous year — superkicked both men in the women's bathroom; Mark Windham then came out of a bathroom stall and clotheslined both men and powerbombed Randalls onto a sink; Timmy Windham and then Troy Windham burst in. The broadcast ran out of time with all of them brawling. No finish in this copy.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "March 4, 1996"

matches.note: Roofed steel cage elimination match, no rules, each man allowed one weapon. Rosenthal's 'Surprise' was revealed as Thomas Dennison. If Eli's team won they got five minutes alone in the cage with Matt Rosenthal; if Rosenthal's team won, Poison Ivy owed him a kiss and ATTAXX regained the IC title. Eliminations: Bandit (pinned by Dennison), Simon Cain (pinned by Dennison), Shotgun Shogun (submitted to Eli), Kamikaze Kid (submitted to the Eliminator hold), Jeff Ruxes (pinned by Dennison), ATTAXX (pinned by Eli), Dennison (pinned by Eli after Poison Ivy kicked ATTAXX and passed Eli her high heel).
Billed as a rematch from the previous week's SPT in Greensboro. Matthews slapped referee Patrick Young, Young shoved him back, and Reno school-boyed him from behind.
Clean scientific match; Technician rolled through a flying bodypress into a cradle.

Billed with a fifteen minute time limit; Sammy Benson erased the '1' from the timekeeper's note, so the bell rang at five minutes and the bout was declared a time limit draw. Anarky had Razorback covered when the bell sounded.
Taped before the broadcast; Benson destroyed the tape, so Buckley recapped it verbally. Won with a backslide; billed as Tidle Wave's CSWA debut.
Billed as LIBERTY & JUSTICE vs FIRE & ICE; taped before the broadcast and recapped verbally. Fire & Ice went on to lose Death Games later the same night.
Two power bombs then the Vipersault. Viper gestured for a belt afterward.

Billed as S & M vs JAPANESE ASSAULT, the third installment of the feud. Shogun threw salt in Seebok's eyes then hit a reverse moonsault off the top. Buckley calls it a tainted victory; Benson notes the match was not no-DQ.

Randalls ambushed Storm and Maxwell Diamond before the bell. Storm missed a moonsault through the Spanish broadcast table; Randalls piledrove him on the wreckage and won by submission with the Devastator, then held it screaming 'Bailey!'

Billed as CS EXPRESS vs MASTERS OF MISERY. Finished with the Rocket Launcher. The Armed Forces, TTL and Ray S. Cornette then destroyed the Express and called them out for Winter's Warriors VII; both men were taken out on stretchers.

Cyborgus interfered repeatedly with the metal arm and Cornette threw in the branding iron. Hornet came down, shoved referee Ben Worthington aside and struck Williams to break the Indian Deathlock; Worthington called for the bell and Williams won by disqualification.

Schmid accompanied by Dr. Marvin Monroe and Billy Ray Moses; Ventolo brought a six pack to the ring, vomited on Wesley Paige and later broke a beer bottle over his head. Schmid cycled through his Teri, Flair and Adler personalities. Brigsby submitted to the Master Lock. Merritt and Thomas then ran in with an attack dog and broke a laptop over Schmid's head.

For the GREENSBORO TITLE. No DQ, with a can of weapons at ringside. Poison Ivy held the title match hostage until Matt Rosenthal served his five minutes with Eli and Bandit; ATTAXX laid both out first, but Eli recovered and put Rosenthal in the Eliminator. ATTAXX chokeslammed Wild Asian on the floor before the bell. Asian retained with a moonsault; Billy Starr then maced him and hit him with the Greensboro belt.

For the PRESIDENTIAL TITLE. Karelin defending, Wright seconded by Ray S. Cornette. Worthington was bumped, Wright's German suplex went uncounted, and Karelin hit a German suplex of his own for the fall.

For the EN/CPUWA WORLD TAG TEAM TITLE. Billed as <> CUTTERS (C) vs TSUNAMI/WILDSTAR, also referred to as NC-17. Enderson rolled through Tsunami's flying bodypress with a handful of tights. Mike Randalls then chaired both Cutters.

For the USN HEAVYWEIGHT TITLE. Michaels defending with Teri Melton, who twice interfered. Windham hit the Lariat and covered, but Hornet hit the ring and pulled him off during the count; the two brawled and Windham eventually left. No ruling is stated in this copy. Windham then piledrove Pedro of the Spanish Broadcast team on the floor.

For the UNIFIED WORLD TAG TEAM TITLE. Billed as THE HORSEMEN (C) vs DISCO EXPRESS. Chain and Samson argued over who would start; Chain smashed the Disco Midget with a bottle of Jack Daniels, Inferno rammed Samson into Chain and rolled Samson up. Buckley and Benson both question whether the match had officially started, but Manuel Juarez awarded the fall and the belts. Samson walked out on Chain afterward; Mike Flair came out to calm him.

Main event, non-title against the US Tag Team Champions, who were accompanied by TTL and Ray S. Cornette. Hornet walked out mid-match believing GUNS had swerved him, then returned after Karelin showed him the replay. Jim Williams came out of the crowd and struck Hornet in the back with the branding iron; Buckley says 'That'll be a DQ!' but no ruling is announced and the broadcast ends with the ring being cleared.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "January 23, 1999"

matches.note: Crippler dominated and finished after about six minutes with the "Crippling Plunge."

Jackson brought a sledgehammer and a table, with his manager Brian Jackson also involved. An unknown man emerged from the curtain, shoved both Jacksons aside and hit Knuckles in the chest with the sledgehammer; with no DQ the referee counted Jackson's pinfall.

Referee Patrick Young was knocked down; a mystery man chokeslammed Blade and draped Cool Moe D's arm over him. Blade plainly had his foot on the bottom rope during the count. Apocalypse then chokeslammed Blade over the top rope and hit Cool Moe D with The Seventh Seal.

Enforcer seconded by Hot Scott and the rest of ES, Harders by Mrs. Beyer. Hot Scott hit Harders' kneecap with brass knuckles and was ejected; Commissioner Chad Merritt then tossed Harders a chair and told the referee to turn around. Merritt afterwards said on headset he wanted Enforcer to know who "the REAL ENFORCER of the CSWA" is.

Ray S. Cornette, still Starr's manager by contract, sent Jaminson out to work over Starr's previously injured neck; Jaminson and Cornette then walked out, giving Starr the win by count-out. Cornette announced he had booked Starr into the opening match at ELVIS LIVES.
Rap Man seconded by The Rap Master. Douglas finished with the THIRD DEGREE BURN.

Apocalypse seconded by Lady Death; Nemesis billed as "Renamed and Retrained by HORNET" and worked the leg with two figure fours. Apocalypse reversed a small package and grabbed a handful of tights for the win. Afterwards Nemesis snapped, throwing Rhubarb Jones out of his seat and banging a chair against the ringpost and his own head.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "February 15, 1996"

matches.note: Taped. Recapped in short form; pinfall at 5:04. Billed as Monster Joe's CSWA debut.
Taped. Cradle at the 3 minute mark; billed as the Technician's return to the ring.
Taped. ATTAXX jumped Euler before the bell and the match lasted thirty-five seconds; he beat Euler afterward and Euler left on a stretcher. Billed as ATTAXX's in-ring debut.
Reno caught Praxis with a small package as he stepped back through the ropes, then escaped before Dr Guggen could dump the bag of poop on him.
Matt Rosenthal came to ringside and put Liontamer's foot on the ropes; Gage won with a small package and chased Rosenthal to the locker room.
Bandit accompanied by Poison Ivy. Starr pinched Ivy and kissed her, drawing her away from the ring, then hit Bandit with one of her high heels while referee Patrick Young was distracted.
Billed as S & M vs Japanese Assault, a rematch from Battle of the Belts XIII. Seebok got his knees up on a moonsault and hit a DDT. ATTAXX attacked both winners afterward and they left on stretchers.

Both men counted out by Patrick Young while brawling on the floor; neither appeared to care. Doctor Silver came out and called the Caretaker off. Billed as Anarky's CSWA debut. No draw or no-contest wording used, so no result field recorded.
Matt Rosenthal interfered repeatedly for Matthews. Jean Claude rolled through a flying bodypress with a handful of tights.
Karelin accompanied by Mad Mike; announcers stress he wrestled it cleanly. German suplex with a bridge for the fall.

Billed as Armed Forces (with TTL and new advisor Ray S. Cornette) vs Disco Express. Disco Midget climbed in and put Submarine in a sleeper; Ben Worthington called for the bell and disqualified the Disco Express. GUNS then ran in to stop Battleship dropping the Atomic Bomb on the Midget.

Schmid accompanied by bodyguard Billy Ray Moses and manager/psychiatrist Dr Marvin Monroe; Storm by Maxwell Diamond. Monroe struck Storm's knee with a mallet and Schmid rolled him up with a handful of tights. Billed as Nathan Storm's CSWA debut. The <>Cutters attacked Schmid afterward until Billy Ray Moses fired a shotgun in the air.
Randalls wearing the Hornet armband he took from GUNS on Death Island. Submission to the Devastator after two piledrivers.

For the GREENSBORO TITLE. Asian defending under stipulations MTV chose, under which a DQ or countout would give MTV the belt. Gladiator, brought in by Dr Silver, choked MTV with piano wire before the bell. Patrick Young ruled the bout a no-contest with Bandit and ATTAXX brawling; announcers state Asian retains.

For the INTRACONTINENTAL TITLE. Eliminator defending, accompanied by Alicia. Hell's Caretaker gestured and Alicia entered the ring and gouged Eli's eyes; Juarez called for the bell and ruled it a disqualification win for the champion. Doc Silver then sprayed Eli with a 'Sleep Stick' of ether and put an 'I'M LIVING THE LIE!' T-shirt on him.

For the UNIFIED WORLD TAG TEAM TITLE. Billed as THE HORSEMEN (C) vs <> CUTTERS, the Cutters accompanied by Maxwell Diamond. Samson pinned Planchard and Enderson pinned Chain simultaneously; Rhubarb Jones announced the ruling and the Horsemen retain.

For the EN WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT TITLE. Main event. The copy breaks off with Melton holding an abdominal stretch and Buckley going to a commercial break; the served document carries the line 'Note: end of match posts lost'. No finish stated.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "May 13, 1998"

matches.note: Watson used a steel chair on the floor and choked Brigsby on the top rope, then won by submission with the swinging full nelson.
A two-by-four and then a baseball bat thrown in from the crowd were used. Referee Patrick Young counted the fall in the aisle.

The document says the two men wanted a roofed steel cage match but CSWA officials would not sanction it. An extension cord was used on Crippler's throat. Crippler ducked the sweet chin music and answered with an insiguire kick.

Billed as the first of three Degeneration Next vs. Elimination Squad matchups. Referee Patrick Young. Hannibal the Cannibal came down with a chair and was confronted by "The Enforcer", then dragged off by Deacon and Preacher while the Shepherd cut a promo on DN. Rap Man won with a running bulldog out of a headlock off the turnbuckle.
Hot Scott and The Enforcer accompanied the Eliminator. Finish was a powerbomb.
Declared a time-limit draw when the twenty-minute limit expired. Referee Patrick Young. A table was used outside and both men ended up in the crowd.

matches.stipulation: Nightclub Street Fight, Disco Ball On A Pole
matches.note: Billed teams: Disco Supreme vs. Disco Express. Held in a ring set up inside a nightclub called Uncle Jesse's, called by Rudy Seitzer on location; to win, a team member had to get the disco ball down from the pole. The drunken Disco Midget turned on Judd Jennrich with an ether-soaked rag; Seitzer concluded the Inferno/Midget split had been a work. Disco Inferno took the ball down.

Billed as Elimination Squad vs. Page Michaels/Da Crack Baby, another Elimination Squad/Degeneration Next confrontation. Eliminator got his second pin of the night on Rap Man, who was tagged in for Michaels, after a spiked piledriver.

Billed teams: Soldier vs. Moral Majority, described as the newly-formed team of the Preacher and Deacon. A masked man in tights reading "EL" ran in with a chair and hit Deacon by accident. Referee Patrick Young. The Shepherd chanted from the apron to bring Deacon around, and Preacher finally pinned Cid Highwind after two standing neckbreakers.

A rematch from PRIMETIME in Puerto Rico. Chairs and a table were used; Corleone missed an elbow off the apron and broke the table himself. Radder hit the FROSTBITE but Corleone kicked out, then won with a top rope DDT.

Billed as Eddy Love's CSWA debut, seconded by Sweet Melissa. Randalls piledrove Sweet Melissa in the ring early and later clotheslined her off the apron. Referee Ben Worthington reached ten with both men brawling in the stands and the document declares a double count-out; no draw or no contest is stated.

For the Unified World Tag Team Championships. Billed teams: SWAT Team (champions) vs. Killer Instinct. Colt chaired Martinez on the floor and Beretta used brass knuckles on Massacre before the Peacemaker. The champions retained.

matches.stipulation: tag team match, First Man To Pin Wins Title
matches.note: For the CSWA World Championship. Special referee Julius Godreign, a CSWA front office employee and former US Champion, with his job on the line. Announced by Rhubarb Jones; a coin toss set GUNS and Troy Windham to start. No pinfall is ever counted: with GUNS covering Troy after the Bionic Knee Lift, Godreign refused to count, jawbreakered GUNS and joined in attacking him. The Frat (Shawn Matthews, Bandit, Scotty Michaels and the Red-Headed Stepbrother) came out, Mike Randalls ran in against them, and Mark Windham cleared the ring with a chair. No winner or ruling is given.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "July 15, 1997"

matches.note: Joined a few minutes in. Starr won by submission with the figure four.
Joined a few minutes in. Melton's return match; his wife Kristy Marie was at ringside. He won by submission with the FIGURE FOUR while holding the top rope for unseen leverage.
Wylder finished with a TOMBSTONE piledriver.
Outlaw attacked from behind before the bell. Bonecrusher finished with the POWERBOMB.

Dream Warrior's CSWA return match. Referee Ben Worthington called for the bell when he saw Spunkmeyer shove a muffin down Dream Warrior's throat during the cover; Spunkmeyer kept force-feeding him muffins afterward.
Referee Ben Worthington. Swift finished with a top rope elbow.
Gant finished with the CRASH AND BURN, his modified Tiger Driver.
Billed teams: the DESTRUCTION CREW vs. LUCHADORO DX, announced by Rhubarb Jones as making their American debut. Referee Patrick Young. Finish was SAKI Gedo's double springboard moonsault.

Grudge match Fiennes asked for. Referee Ben Worthington was knocked out; Jason "Wildside" Wylder ran in, DDT'd Fiennes and draped Wildstar over him, then revived the referee. Wylder attacked both men with a 2x4 afterward.

No result is declared. Godreign blindsided Randalls with the US title belt before the bell; the brawl went through a table and chairs on the floor. Randalls refused to release the Devastor after Godreign passed out, ignoring the referee's count, and was pulled off by five or six security officers, clubbed and handcuffed. Commissioner Merritt announced Randalls was suspended from the CSWA.

Impromptu match made when JT Tyler issued an open challenge to the dressing room after his contract signing was announced; Hornet answered. Referee Ben Worthington called for the bell. No result: after a double clothesline and a standing ten-count the two men spoke, Worthington called for a microphone, and the match was stopped by mutual agreement. Buckley called it an exhibition and said THE ALLIANCE was back together.

For the CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP. Announced by Rhubarb Jones as one fall with a sixty minute time limit. Referee Patrick Young was flattened between GUNS and the turnbuckle after Windham pulled him into the path. Javid Dones jawed with Windham throughout from a ringside seat; Junior Hornet chaired GUNS; Timmy Windham bungeed in; Mark Windham piledrove Troy and was fought off by HEAT. With Young out, Hornet came to the ring and counted the fall himself. Commissioner Chad Merritt ruled from the booth that the result stood.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "August 8, 1995"

matches.note: Billed as the Eagle's CSWA debut.
Both billed as new to the CSWA; Savage finished with a DDT after about ten minutes.
Tsunami's partner in crime WILDSTAR worked Day over on the floor before Tsunami finished with a Reverse Moonsault.

The Beachcombers are named as The Hawaiian Hurrican and the Big Kahuna, with Mad Mike. No 'Winner:' line is printed for this match; the write-up says only that they 'wasted no time in dispelling BIG PUNISHMENT, who failed to dish out any', and Buckley follows with 'Mad Mike's boys...are back on their game'.
Finish was a tombstone piledriver; billed as a debut.
Billed as the Minutemen's CSWA debut, a tag team force in the NWC; five minutes.
First of Mike Roiter's two matches on the card; finish was the ROITER LINE.

Second of three Rosenthal Family challenge matches to the Roiters. Alex Roiter had the masked man beaten but took the microphone and refused to pin him, saying he knew who was behind the mask; he was chaired from behind on his way out, brought back and pinned. This masked man's identity is not revealed.

Final Rosenthal/Roiter challenge match. Roiter hit the ROITER LINE and the masked man kicked out — only the second man ever to do so, after Mark Windham — then stood up, laughed and unmasked as 'Mr. Magnificent' Tom Adler. About 45 minutes; Adler finished with the ADLERPLEX.
Billed as another NWC star's big-league debut.

No 'Winner:' line is printed. The write-up says Taylor 'didn't need too much time to defeat Avery'. Billed as Avery Lincoln's return from a neck injury suffered in the AAWC. Afterwards Tom Adler met Taylor at the entrance way and officials had to separate them, building to their SUMMER HEAT match.
Brigsby, now managed by Mad Mike, finished with a reverse neckbreaker for his second straight win.
Debut for the Haskells, William and Timothy Haskell, a team brought in by Steven Flair, who was at ringside. Finish was the Haskell Drop.
Finish was a powerslam reversed into a small package.
Dwyer billed as undefeated since entering the CSWA; Studd finished with a brainbuster and a DDT.
Ultimate Defender billed as the Greensboro Champ, Dementia as one of the CORPORATION's thugs and undefeated to date; finish was a reversed german suplex and a bridge.

Pamela and Scotty Michaels seconded Tropic, Poison Ivy the Eliminator, and the two women fought throughout. Tropic brought his guitar in and had it used on him. After the bell Scotty Michaels entered the cage, kicked the Eliminator, threw a bucket of water on him and pushed him into the live cage.

matches.stipulation: 1 fall, no time limit, no disqualifications, no count-out, weapons allowed
matches.note: GUNS attacked The Chosen One from behind with a chair before the bell; Hornet, confused, brainbustered him on the concrete, beat him with Sammy Benson's microphone and pinned him. Afterwards Hornet called out GUNS for Disney Days.

Billed as PERFECT ALLIANCE vs ARROGENCE, Arrogence led by Teri Melton and billed as the No.1 contenders for the US Tag belts. Scotty Waters introduced Steel Viper and Degadeth as the alliance's two new members, stayed at ringside, elbowed Wright and later chaired Joey Melton in the back of the head for the win. Referee Jorge Gonzales.

Bonecrusher billed as the USN Champ and 'the man to break Mark's shoulder'; referee Felipe Rodriquez. Windham reversed a corner charge into a roll-up for the win, then was beaten down and busted open by Steven Flair with Cyborgus, Dementia and Ray Steckler.

1 fall, 30 minute time limit; Woods billed as having beaten GUNS before. Hornet ran down and laid Woods out with a press slam and a Shooting Star Press before the bell, mirroring what GUNS had done earlier; GUNS then finished with a belly to belly. Buckley notes this had been due to be for the EN title until Tom Adler took it.

name: CSWA SuperPRIMETIME POOLJAM in Nassau -- August 17, 1999

date.source: the document's own dateline, "August 17, 1999"

matches.note: Recap paragraph. El Nino, 'formerly known as the Mexican Muppet,' finishes with a 360 splash off the top.
Recap paragraph. The winning team is billed as SIMPLY STUNNING. Hardy reverses the figure four and Marcus Delmar taps. Referee Patrick Young.
Recap paragraph. Grossard finishes with a fallaway slam and a big powerslam.
Recap paragraph. Martin, formerly known as Cool Moe D, counters a figure four attempt into a small package. Buckley notes Martin 'seemed... distracted by something.'
Recap paragraph. Commando finishes with a legdrop and a victory roll.
Recap paragraph. Jackson submits to a Boston Crab rather than risk serious injury.
Solomon hooks THE CRUCIFIER and referee Manny Juarez awards the match after checking the arm.

For the CSWA Greensboro Title. Blade wins with the GUILLOTINE BLADE. Buckley insists Douglas had a foot on the rope and was robbed; the announced decision stands. Blade grabs the belt and leaves before Douglas can argue.

For the CSWA United States Heavyweight Championship. Champion Randy Harders is eliminated first when Nemesis hits the Absolute Zero and BOTH Nemesis and Radder cover him for the three. Nemesis then pins Radder by stepping into an attempted Victory Roll. Referee Manny Juarez. Nemesis becomes a two-time US Champion.

Impromptu handicap match; the masked Peacekeeper drops from the ceiling on a zipline and calls out 'some big competition,' and The New Big Connection answers. Peacekeeper powerslams the 538-pound Slack onto Parsons and referee Ben Worthington counts the double pin. Billed as his in-ring debut.

matches.stipulation: Street-fight rules, fought in the Parsons Cruise Liner parking lot after the boat docked
matches.note: Billed as a rematch to determine the top contender to the Greensboro Title. Referee Pee Wee Troutman. With both men out, five CSWA jobbers -- Carl Brigsby, Wesley Page, La Psychotica and the tag team Abercrombie and Finch -- come out of the crowd and destroy Wylde with a double Rock Bottom on a car hood; Brigsby then rolls Stanley on top for the count.

matches.note: Billed as a double debut match. Jackson finished it at the ten minute mark with "The Hostile Takeover!"
Delmar got the pin at the nine minute mark with a powerbomb and a handful of tights.
Steele hooked in submission moves until the referee had to call the match. The recap's phrase "This one was no contest from the beginning" is rhetorical - a winner is declared.
Gettis won with a flying bodypress.

Scheduled singles match. Before the bell Troy Windham offered a tag match instead - Beretta and Torrance against Bandit and Junior Hornet - and Beretta accepted, then attacked Torrance's knee from behind. Bandit chokeslammed Torrance, Junior Hornet stomped him, and Troy Windham slapped the mat three times himself. No official ruling was announced and no referee is named.
The bell rang signalling the end of the match. The result line reads "WINNER:Time Lime Draw" - an apparent typo for Time Limit Draw.
Harders hit a brainbuster and a DDT for the three count.

Cardigo Mysterian, hired by Thornton Squeezefeld to help his son, entered the ring, then turned and decked Ill Squeeze with the corner of his briefcase, busting him open. Referee Pee Wee Troutman awarded the match to Ill Squeeze by disqualification; Douglas could not believe the decision.
Ran more than twenty five minutes. Silky Rose shot a fireball straight up in the air as a distraction; Inferno dropped Martin on his head out of a choke lift right before Troutman called for the DQ.
Former tag team partners. Cruise, under the direction of his new manager Mercades Devon, hit the "Crippling Plunge."

Billed as the CSWA stateside debut of two WAR (Japan) stars and the return of former United States Champion HEAT. Referee Patrick Young gave a standing ten-count to Grossard and HEAT, then gave the win to Kerrigan.

matches.stipulation: TRINIDAD TORNADO Match - No Disqualification/Falls Count Anywhere
matches.note: Dexter ambushed Stanley disguised as a crew member. The fight went backstage; Lance Richards powerbombed Stanley through the sound and light board before Dexter hit a cradle brainbuster and referee Manuel Juarez counted three.

matches.stipulation: "The Blade Invitational" battle royal - Winner receives Greensboro Title shot
matches.note: Six men. Delmar eliminated first by Gettis; Havoc and Wicked Sight, then Jackson, then Gettis went out; Sight and Commando both went over the top together and Sight caught the middle rope while Commando's feet hit the floor.
Referee Ben Worthington. Deacon pinned Alex Wylde with the Altar Call. Nemesis and Commando came to ringside and attacked Wylde afterward; Rob Sampson then turned and attacked Wylde as well.

For the CSWA WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP. Chaotic finish. Referee Manuel Juarez was knocked out; Sunshine Del Payne entered the ring and counted a three on Love for Flair. Juarez then revived, ignored that fall, and instead disqualified Eddy Love for a chairshot he had taken from Love roughly twenty minutes earlier. Flair retains. Both men bled; the two went through a table off the top turnbuckle; a nine-man brawl involving the No Limit Soldiers (Troy Windham, Junior Hornet, Bandit), the Unholy (Apocalypse, Pat Black, Rob Sampson) and Kevin Powers broke out around the finish.

Royal Fashion billed as Sir Dunton and The Model; Masked Assassins as Scope and Bullet. Finished with the Sniper's Bullet - Bullet's sharpshooter plus Scope's top-rope leg drop.
Melton's return, with new manager MISS HOOTERS at ringside. He offered a handshake then kicked Bramble in the midsection; Bramble submitted to the Figure Four.

For the Enterprises World Championship. Billed as Randalls's first EN World Championship title defence. The match never started: a 'fan' threw a drink on HEAT in the aisle, then Randalls hit him with a two-by-four and broke a glass bottle over his head, leaving him bleeding and taken out by ambulance. Buckley: 'Randalls will retain his EN Title, however.' No bell, no decision.

For the CSWA Presidential Championship. One-fall match set by the Board of Directors for the title, vacated during the last European Tour. Buckley openly calls the pairing rigged. Finished with a Pearl of the Orient.

For the Unified Tag Team Titles. MUPPET MANIA billed as champions Muppet Kid and the Mexican Muppet; the Roiters as Alex and Bubba, wrestling their final CSWA match. Muppet Kid pinned Alex Roiter after nailing him with his bungee cord; the referee then saw the cord, reversed the call and raised the Roiters' hands. 'MUPPET MANIA has been disqualified for the use of the "Muppet Maneuver," but they will retain the Unified Titles.' The champions lose the match and keep the belts.

matches.note: Opening bout signed by Ray S. Cornette under his contract with Starr. Starr grabbed Cornette by the throat on the apron and Brigsby hit him with a chair; Patrick Young disqualified Brigsby.
Second match signed on the spot by Cornette. Starr finished with a facebuster and a cover.
Third match signed on the spot by Cornette. Starr blocked Jaminson's brass knuckles, used them himself, then tossed them to Cornette before the referee turned around, and covered with a grapevine.

Radder seconded by Kelly; Silky Rose did not appear with Inferno. Inferno was disqualified for throwing Radder over the top rope, then continued the beating with a tombstone piledriver on the floor and threw Radder into the ring steps. Radder got up bleeding and challenged him to come back.

matches.stipulation: Scaffold match, billed as "From Heaven To Hell"; to win, one man must knock his opponent off a platform suspended 30 fee
matches.note: Black seconded by Lady Death, Deacon by The Shepherd. Deacon caught Black's head with his feet out of a powerbomb attempt and Frank'n'Parsons'd him off the scaffold, going over himself but catching the edge.

For the Greensboro Heavyweight Championship. Apocalypse seconded by Lady Death. Douglas finished with a guillotine leg drop from the top. Randy Harders then climbed out from under the ring with a baseball bat, cracked Douglas in the back, hit the Whirlwind and proclaimed himself number one contender.

matches.stipulation: Both managers, Disco Midget and Ray S. Cornette, suspended above the ring in a steel cage; ruled Texas Tornado rules on
matches.note: For the UNIFIED TAG TEAM CHAMPIONSHIPS. Billed as two-time champions Disco Express defending against three-time champions ARROGANCE. Cornette stomped the Disco Midget's fingers loose and the Midget fell from the cage onto Joey Melton's ribs; Disco Inferno followed with an elbow drop for the three count.

matches.stipulation: TRIANGLE MATCH; first man to get a pinfall wins the strap; ruled no disqualification, 60 minute time limit
matches.note: For the United States Championship. Powers seconded by Steve Radder carrying an "Extreme" belt, Eliminator by Hot Scott, Flair by Poison Ivy. Radder hit Flair with the Extreme belt and Ivy caned Radder; Flair shoved Eliminator fifteen feet off the top through a table, then beat Powers with Powers' own finisher.

matches.stipulation: TEXAS DEATH MATCH; 60 minute time limit; the fight goes on until one man cannot answer the 10 count; pinfalls count anyw
matches.note: Mid-match Timmy Windham appeared alive, wheeling Mickey Benedict to the aisle. Windham chased them backstage, where Benedict hit him with a fireball and Timmy broke a concrete block over his head. Hornet, apparently unaware, dropped an elbow and a shooting star press from an air conditioning vent, and Ben Worthington counted Windham out.

matches.stipulation: CAGE MATCH, one fall with no time limit
matches.note: For the CSWA World Heavyweight Championship. Love seconded by Sweet Melissa, Vizzack by Poison Ivy and, after she and Arthur fell from the catwalk into the ring before the bell, Sunshine Del Payne. Hornet barred PLR from ringside. Kevin Powers and Sweet Melissa hooked a generator's jumper cables to the cage; Love's arm hit the electrified cage before Vizzack finished with the Daredevil Flyer.

matches.note: Starman's CSWA re-debut after an extended absence; a sunset flip off the top. 'Starman gets the quick and easy victory.'

Bishop Hell billed as a member of the Doom Team, formerly the Rosenthal Family. DMW dropped him seven feet out of the backbreaker and hooked both legs; 'Devil's Masked Warrior continues his unbeaten streak since his return.' Ref Ben Worthington.
Both billed CSWA rookies; Woods undefeated coming in and billed a two-time AGWA World Champion. Finished with a belly to belly suplex.

Jean Claude accompanied by his new manager Matt Rosenthal, who slapped Nace's hands off the ropes, hit him with a shoe and then chaired him. Both men fought outside with chairs. 'There's the bell!  This one will be a double count-out.' CSWA officials had to break it up. Ref Ben Worthington.

The Rosenthal Family's advertised 'Secret Team' is revealed at the bell as BIG PUNISHMENT - MR BIG and the SUPER PUNISHER, managed by Matt Rosenthal, with Dr. Coge and Suzuki in the corner. Tex was powerbombed then splashed from the top by Mr Big; Chico was tackled out of the ring. 'Tex is having convulsions.'

Referee William Dibble was knocked down in the corner. 'Hot' Johnny Tropic ran in, chaired the Eliminator off the top rope, rolled Degadeth on top of him, then revived the groggy referee, who counted the fall. 'The Eliminator is robbed of the win by Johnny Tropic!' The announced result stands.
Sexy Boys billed as Steven Miller and Larry Martin; Japanese Nightmares as the Great Buddah and the Shadow Dancer, managed by Matt Rosenthal. Martin's arm dropped three times in the weaverlock.

Southern Twist billed as the Karate Kid and Too Tall Tom. The Roiters never made the ring: Bubba Roiter was attacked backstage by 'Hot' Johnny Tropic with a two-by-four and a set of wall lockers pushed over on him. 'the ref has counted the Roiters out, and Southern Twist will get the count-out win.' Buckley had earlier corrected the line-up to say Mike and Bubba, not Alex.

Billed to determine the number one contenders to the United States Tag Team Titles, currently held by The Alliance (JT Tyler and Hornet). Wright and Melton are billed together as ARROGANCE; Johnny Gunn is making his wrestling debut and is billed as the cousin of 'Equalizer' Eddie Gunn. Melton kneed HEAT through the ropes and Gunn submitted to Wright's STF. Afterwards HEAT beat his own partner down in the middle of the ring.

matches.stipulation: WORLD LEAGUE match, to determine the #1 seed in the World League International Heavyweight Championship Tournament
matches.note: Billed as the WORLD LEAGUE's Pay-Per-View debut. Mitchell accompanied by The Mastermind, Pierce by Bill the Banker. The first referee was knocked out; the replacement who ran down and counted the winning fall was 'Hot' Johnny Tropic in disguise, unmasked when Pierce cold-cocked him and his glasses and hat flew off. The Mastermind had also hit Pierce with a shoe. Stan Parsons later reports 'we have heard nothing from CS Enterprises about whether that match will stand.'

For the Greensboro Heavyweight title. Jackson pinned the champion after hitting him with a pair of brass knuckles the Ultimate Dragon had left in the ring, and was announced as the NEW champion; referee Pee Wee Troutman then saw the knuckles, called for the bell, disqualified Jackson and awarded the belt back to the Ultimate Defender, who retains. David Simmons and the Sniper were at ringside 'to assure this match of a clean ending' and took the Ultimate Dragon out. Buckley disputes the call: 'But, he didn't....'

For the CSWA's United States/National Heavyweight Championship. Rematch; the two brawled on the floor before the bell. Bonecrusher hit a top-rope belly to back, a tombstone, a top-rope shoulderblock and the powerbomb before finishing with the Implant DDT. Ref Ben Worthington awarded him the belt.

For the World Tag Team Title. The Berzerk Beachcombers - the Big Kahuna and the Hawaiian Hurricane, managed by Mad Mike - defending against Mark Windham and Junior HORNET, who brought the Mighty Morphin Midgets to ringside. Mad Mike pulled the top rope down on Junior HORNET; the Big Kahuna used a chain on Windham; the Midgets hit a Midget Rocket Launcher and finally the Red Morphin Midget broke a coconut over the Big Kahuna's head, letting Junior HORNET turn the sunset flip over for the fall.

matches.note: Heartbreaker played possum and finished with a Super Kick. Anarky's bodyguard Thomas "The Machine" Gunn sat at ringside scouting, helped Heartbreaker back into the ring at one point, and traded words with Gage.
Reno, billed as an ex United States/National Champion, was busted open early on the ringpost and came back to win with a superplex.
Rhubarb Jones billed him as Rocky Ford Meloneer, from Rocky Mountain, Colorado; Wolf from parts unknown. Finish was the Cantaloupe Crush, described as a double arm DDT.

The Executioner was managed by "Deathdoll" Kristi, who saved one pinfall by putting his foot on the ropes and repeatedly distracted the Dragon. The Executioner accidentally struck Kristi with a double axe-handle and was rolled up while staring at her.
TNT (Theodore N. Titus) was accompanied by the Big Brain, who shook the ropes to crotch Collins on the top turnbuckle. Collins still won with a powerbomb.

Vai badly injured his knee missing a dive into the ring barrier; Virile worked the leg, applied a figure four, and finished with the Perfect Plex. Virile also billed as "Primetime" and as the former Mirror Image.

matches.note: Sonya DDT'd Christopher onto a chair on the floor, opening her up badly, then won with a sleeper after Ben Worthington's third arm drop. Tia Bonds seconded Christopher.

matches.note: Conner finished with a brainbuster followed by a superplex.

matches.stipulation: Greensboro Tournament, second round of the winners bracket
matches.note: The on-page header for this bout is mislabelled "Round 1 Winners Bracket"; the commentary introduces it as the second round. Meloneer won again with the Cantaloupe Crush.

matches.stipulation: Greensboro Tournament, second round of the winners bracket
matches.note: Header is mislabelled "Round 1 Winners Bracket" and mis-names Virile as "The Original Xavier Collins". Collins wrestled most of the match with what the announcers called a broken nose after a headbutt; Virile finished with a top-rope flying crossbody to the floor and a cover back inside.

Ruled a double count-out and both men eliminated from the tournament after a brawl on the floor involving the ring bell, a chair and exposed concrete; "Deathdoll" Kristi led Wolf into an ambush. Clint Collins received a bye as a result. No winner declared.
Vai hobbled to the ring on the knee hurt in his first match and was attacked before the bell; he stole it with a small package.

For the CSWA Intra-Continental Championship. TNT ran in, chaired and piledrove Windsor; Ben Worthington called for the bell. Windsor won by disqualification but the Wild Asian kept the belt. Afterwards TNT said Windsor had cost him the NWC World Championship and Windsor dove on him from the ring.
The other second-round losers bracket match was a bye for Clint "Critical Mass" Collins. Vai, still limping, countered out of a piledriver and hit a DDT.

matches.stipulation: Tag team match to UNIFY the Enterprise World Tag Team Titles and the Unified World Tag Team Championships; wrestled as a
matches.note: For the Enterprise World Tag Team Titles and Unified World Tag Team Championships. Troy Windham defended the EN World Tag belts alone after Shawn Matthews threw the belts in a trash can and quit Generation X-Press. Titles could change on a count-out or disqualification. Matt Rosenthal managed the Japanese Assault and repeatedly distracted Windham. Shogun Slam finished it.

matches.stipulation: SPECIAL TRIANGLE CHALLENGE MATCH, elimination, one hour time limit
matches.note: Originally scheduled for the Enterprises World Championship; made non-title after GUNS' protests. Windham was eliminated first, disqualified for attacking GUNS with a rifle butt that Sammy Benson said a mysterious woman in a long coat handed him at ringside. Anarky then pinned GUNS with a Shooting Star Press. GUNS carried a bottle of urine to the ring as his own 'Enterprises World Championship'.

matches.stipulation: WAR GAMES: THE MATCH BEYOND, SUBMISSION OR SURRENDOR, two rings under two cages
matches.note: America's Team versus the X-Change. Pinfalls did not count and submissions only counted once War Games proper began; a 20-sided die decided the man advantage, which the X-Change won. America's Team entered a man short and Mike Randalls appeared unannounced as their fifth man, having been shown earlier being released from the Green Valley Institution. Randalls produced a taser from his boot and shocked Thomas Knight until Knight surrendered; referee Pee Wee Troutman called for the bell. Adler used a metal rod on HORNET's knee throughout.

matches.stipulation: Special challenge match with the ownership of the CSWA and one million dollars on the line
matches.note: Maxwell Diamond never appeared, having been taken away in an ambulance after America's Team's post-War Games five minutes with him, so Thomas Knight wrestled it alone. Jon "Cruncher" Katz ran in with a baseball bat and struck Stephen Thomas in the knee; the referee called for the bell. No winner is announced, but Buckley states CS Enterprises keeps the league and that Knight had looked to have it won.

matches.stipulation: CSWA United States Heavyweight Championship Tournament, first round
matches.note: Windham had the Sharpshooter on when Timmy Windham stormed the aisle; Mark broke the hold to argue with him, threw a right hand that Timmy blocked, and took a kick to the head that dropped him into Eliminator's Double Arm Powerbomb. Referee Ben Worthington counted three.

matches.stipulation: CSWA United States Heavyweight Championship Tournament, first round
matches.note: Merritt had ruled Radder would get a bye if Vizzack was not present. Julius Kessler broke the referee's standing count by jumping on the apron and brawling with Radder, and Vizzack came in through the crowd in street clothes at the count of eight with Sunshine. Finished with the DAREDEVIL FLYER. Benson notes Radder has grounds for complaint over Kessler's interference.

matches.stipulation: CSWA United States Heavyweight Championship Tournament, first round
matches.note: Apocalypse came out with Black, put Black's foot on the bottom rope to break a count, and cracked Deacon in the back of the head with a chair after Black had pulled referee Ben Worthington into the path of Deacon's top-rope shoulderblock. Buckley calls it highway robbery.

matches.stipulation: CSWA United States Heavyweight Championship Tournament, first round
matches.note: Preacher accompanied by the Shepherd; Powers by Gina and Susan. Susan distracted referee Ben Worthington and Gina raked the Preacher's eyes; Powers then produced a small chain, choked the Preacher into a pinning position and got the three count with his leg on the middle rope.

For the CSWA UNIFIED TAG-TEAM CHAMPIONSHIP of the WORLD. ARROGANCE is Peyton Wright and Joey Melton, billed as eight-time World Tag-Team Champions and led by Ray S. Cornette; Disco Express is Boogie Man and Disco Inferno with the Disco Midget. Ray S. Cornette got in with the tennis racket and hit Joey Melton as well as Boogie Man; the Disco Midget then tackled Cornette and beat him with the racket. Referee Ben Worthington rang the bell and Rhubarb Jones announced a double disqualification; the champions keep the titles.

matches.stipulation: CSWA United States Heavyweight Championship Tournament, semifinal
matches.note: Eliminator knocked Apocalypse off the apron, then hit a powerbomb and a Tombstone Piledriver; referee Patrick Young counted three. Lady Mo is described as being in Eliminator's corner.

matches.stipulation: CSWA United States Heavyweight Championship Tournament, semifinal
matches.note: Ray S. Cornette made a phone call on Powers's signal and the masked Eddy Love ran out, chaired Julius Kessler unconscious and grabbed Vizzack while Gina and Susan held and slapped Sunshine. Cornette held referee Patrick Young's shirt and threw in his cell phone, which Powers shattered over Vizzack's head before hooking the figure four; Young looked at the unconscious Vizzack and called for the bell, giving Powers the submission victory.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, FINAL FOUR semifinal
matches.note: Starr accompanied by Sweet Melissa. Sparks pulled a table out from under the ring and set it up; a Starr back drop sent Sparks over the top and through his own table, which referee Patrick Young ruled incidental contact, and Starr then powerbombed him on the remnants before the pin. Afterwards Teri Melton came down and brawled with Sweet Melissa, and Poison Ivy came out of the crowd and fought them both, tearing away part of Melissa's dress before Starr covered her with his ring robe.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, FINAL FOUR semifinal
matches.note: Hornet wrestled with his eyes damaged from the pre-show Raid attack. He had the Scorpion Deathlock on when Sweet Melissa distracted referee Ben Worthington and the masked man rolled out from under the ring, threw powder or spray in Hornet's eyes and hit a neckbreaker; Love then hit the HURRICANE PILEDRIVER for the three count.

matches.stipulation: CSWA United States Heavyweight Championship Tournament, final
matches.note: For the UNITED STATES HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPIONSHIP. Powers came out demanding a forfeit because Eliminator, limping from a left-knee injury inflicted off camera, could hardly walk, and grabbed the belt to have himself announced champion; Eliminator attacked him from behind. Powers worked the knee with a figure four around the ring post and a chair, and after Eliminator's knee gave out on a top-rope dive Powers hooked the figure four and referee Patrick Young called for the bell. Buckley calls it a tainted win; Eliminator was seconded by Hot Scott, the Rap Master and the Rap Man.

matches.stipulation: CSWA World Heavyweight Championship Tournament final; one fall with a sixty-minute time limit
matches.note: For the CSWA World Heavyweight Championship. MAIN EVENT, an all-CORPORATION final worked cleanly with repeated clean breaks; Love with Sweet Melissa, Starr with Teri Melton. Starr set Love backwards on the turnbuckle for a top-rope powerbomb, but Love hooked his head on the way down and turned it into a DDT, then rolled over for the cover. Referee Ben Worthington. Love checked on Starr afterwards and raised his arm along with the belt.

Karelin's second match back to back. Flair's right shoulder was driven into the ringpost and he wrestled the rest of the night injured; Karelin also chaired Ray S. Cornette. Karelin won with the Russian Sickle. 20 points to Karelin.

Karelin's fourth and final match; he won with the Russian Sickle and finished the tournament on 40 points.

The match header bills Randalls as 'Mark Randalls'; every other reference on the card, including the announcers during this match, calls him Mike Randalls. Randalls worked Flair's injured right shoulder and won with the Devestator as Cornette dived in too late. Randalls to 40 points; Flair finished his four matches on 20 and was eliminated.
Windham won with a small package from behind. Both men level on 40 points with one match each remaining.

Hornet worked GUNS' corner. Hornet repeatedly interfered against Windham — holding his leg during a count-out, then dragging him out and attacking him — and the referee called for the bell and awarded Windham a disqualification win worth 10 points, mathematically eliminating GUNS. GUNS confronted Hornet afterwards; Hornet raised both arms in apology and GUNS walked off.

For the EN WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP. Final match of the tournament. Randalls needed a pinfall or count-out win to take the title on points; GUNS was already eliminated but wrestled the match out, including a piledriver on the exposed concrete. Randalls reversed a shoulderbreaker cover into the winning three count and took the tournament with 60 points and a third EN World Championship. GUNS offered a handshake afterwards; the document does not say whether Randalls accepted.

matches.note: Fizzbin's first in-ring test, with Eli Flair and Poison Ivy at ringside as his trainer and manager. Brigsby took the early edge and hit a DDT; Fizzbin rolled outside before the cover, came back with a tornado DDT and a moonsault, and finished with The Monkeywrench, a heel kick from the top rope. This match is narrated in summary rather than called move by move.
Lang finished with a german suplex from the top rope. Cisco was taken out by the medical staff afterwards holding his neck.

date.source: the document's own dateline, "November 21, 1998"

matches.note: Billed as the debut of a brand new wrestler. The Ball Player came to the ring in a baseball uniform and finished with a top rope head butt.

Harders accompanied by Mrs. Beyer, Rap Man by Hot Scott. Enforcer entered the ring with a chair and Hot Scott tried to enter; referee Patrick Young called no DQ. Rap Man submitted to the Whirlwind, a spinning Torture Rack.
Billed as a double debut match. Ruiner finished with the INCESTICIDE.

Billed as Gina and Susan vs. Poison Ivy and Mystery Partner; Ivy revealed Sunshine Del Payne as her partner. Kevin Powers, then Eddy Love with a chair, then Mark Vizzack all entered the ring area. Sunshine pinned Gina with a superkick, her first win.

Billed as ARROGANCE and Ray S. Cornette vs. Disco Express and Disco Midget, and announced by Rhubarb Jones as a MIXED Six-man Tag Team Event. Disco Express were the reigning UNIFIED Tag Team Champions but the belts were not stated to be at stake. Randall Jaminson used brass knuckles and threw the Disco Midget; Ray S. Cornette smashed a cell phone over Boogie Man's head for the finish.

Eli Flair and Kevin Powers, watching at ringside, stormed the ring and attacked Eliminator; referee Ben Worthington called for the bell and awarded the match to Eliminator by disqualification. Flair caned Hot Scott and Eliminator; Powers hit Kiss The Canvas.

Billed as Apocalypse and Pat Black vs. Destruction Crew. Lady Death distracted referee Pee Wee Troutman; Apocalypse used a steel chair. The Deacon's arrival interrupted the finish, with Black covering and Apocalypse hitting The Seventh Seal on Chainsaw.

For the United States Heavyweight Championship. Ring ropes replaced with five layers of barbed wire; no countout, no disqualification, pinfall or submission only. The Elimination Squad ran in and Powers and Flair briefly fought them off together, before Powers hit Flair with the US Title belt and pinned him. Susan held Poison Ivy during the count.

matches.stipulation: Tag team match in which whoever scores the pinfall is awarded the World Championship
matches.note: For the CSWA World Heavyweight Championship. Vizzack named Billy Starr as his mystery partner; Starr refused to co-operate and struck Vizzack. Vizzack pulled the mask off Masked Love to reveal Steve Radder. Hornet, on crutches, returned and hit Eddy Love with a steel crutch, and Ben Worthington called for the bell.

matches.note: Aaron Douglas entered under his masked "El Volcano" gimmick. Blade and Inferno left together.

Billed as Moral Majority vs. Black's Army. Apocalypse arrived late and appeared in the ring only after the lights went out. Silky Rose came to ringside dressed as a nun and drew Deacon away; Dante Inferno chokeslammed Deacon in the aisle, and Apocalypse rolled Preacher up holding the tights.

matches.note: Harders accompanied by Mrs. Beyer. Hot Scott and Rap Man drew referee Ben Worthington to the outside, and Enforcer came out of the crowd and hit Nemesis with a steel chair, leaving Harders to cover.

matches.note: StreetFight rules. LANCE LIEZURE WON. He controlled almost the whole bout -- a DDT on his own skateboard, the steel steps, the guardrail, a chair -- and finished with the Liezure Suite, an old-style rocker dropper onto a chair, referee Manny Juarez counting three. matches.title: cswa-unified-world-tag-team
matches.note: "HOUSE of PAIN," a four-way steel cage match for the Unified Tag Team Titles, one man entering every three minutes and no eliminations until all eight are in. SIMPLY STUNNING RETAINED. The New Suicide Squad went first, RJ Mills covering Tsunami after Nathan Storm put Tsunami off the top of the cage with a FrankenParsons; Raw Deal went next, Michael Hardy hooking WJ Mills into a FrankenParsons cradle; and the deciding fall came when Simon Wilcox threw Hardy off the top of the cage onto both Professionals with a Rocket Launcher and Hardy covered. Referee Pee Wee Troutman. Staged in full on part four of the card.

"Top Contenders Battle Royal": six men, elimination by pinfall or over the top rope, the winner earning the first CSWA World Championship shot after ANNIVERSARY. WICKED SIGHT WON. The order out was Cameron Cruise (over the top, by Shane Southern and Triple X), Apocalypse (over the top off a double superkick by Wicked Sight and Triple X), Triple X (over the top off a reverse elbow by Wicked Sight), Shane Southern (by Tom Adler) and Tom Adler (back body drop to the floor by Wicked Sight). Referee Ben Worthington. Staged in full on part three of the card.

"Rage in the Cage," an I QUIT match inside a steel cage. ELI FLAIR WAS AWARDED THE MATCH, AND REJECTED IT. Neither man said the words; Eddy Love climbed in and threw a towel in for Troy Windham, and referee Patrick Young elected to accept it, the ring announcer stating the ruling in terms. Flair refused to have his arm raised, chokeslammed the referee and said "nobody won that match." Staged in full on part seven of the card.

Billed as a "Mystery Tag Match" with neither partner named beforehand. EDDY LOVE AND GUNS WON. The card stages the reveal on the page: Love's first "partners" are two unnamed midgets, Mark Windham walks out and tags himself into Mike Randalls's corner uninvited, and a masked man then puts Randalls down with a chair and finally powerbombs him off the top rope, Love covering. The masked man unmasks on the middle rope as GUNS, back after nearly four years. Referee Patrick Young. Staged in full on part eight of the card. This replaces a reading that had been recorded as presumed from a later promo; the card itself now carries it.

matches.stipulation: "Rage In The Cage" -- an I QUIT match inside a steel cage, no pinfall, no count-out, no disqualification, and the submission having to happen inside the ring
matches.note: THE DECISION IS DISPUTED ON THE CARD ITSELF, AND BY THE WINNER. Neither man said the words. Troy Windham, wrestling without medical clearance on a signed waiver, had his hand broken against the guardrail with a chair and two fingers snapped one at a time, and refused each time. Eddy Love came to ringside, climbed into the cage and threw a bloodied towel at referee Patrick Young, who called for the bell: the ring announcer states the ruling in terms -- "even though there has been no confirmation of Troy Windham saying the words, 'I QUIT,' referee Patrick Young has elected to accept as an alternative, Eddy Love throwing in the towel." Eli Flair refused to let his arm be raised, chokeslammed the referee, and told the interviewer "Troy didn't say it, so he didn't lose. If Troy didn't lose, I didn't win... nobody won that match." The official's ruling is recorded as the result and the winner's own rejection of it is recorded with it.

matches.note: EDDY LOVE AND GUNS WON, and the card stages the unmasking on the page. Love's first "partners" were two unnamed midgets, one a spoof of his opponent and one dressed as a psychiatrist, who set up a fold-out table in the corner and mimed a therapy session before Randalls chokeslammed one of them through it. Mark Windham walked out mid-match to the Close Encounters theme, climbed into Randalls's corner uninvited and eventually tagged himself in over Randalls's objection. A masked man then came up the ring steps, put Randalls down with a chair and Windham down with two more, powerbombed Randalls, and finally powerbombed him again off the top rope; Love covered for the three. The masked man pulled off the mask on the middle rope and was GUNS, back in the federation after nearly four years. Referee Patrick Young.
